articleTitle: Coating Based Wearable Disc-Shaped Textile Array Antenna for Wireless Body Area Network
abstract: This paper focuses with the design of a wearable textile disc-shaped array antenna for use in wireless body area network (WBAN) communications developed based on a coating technique. Textile materials provide the necessary wearability and flexibility, allowing the antenna to be worn on the body. The proposed array antenna consists of three layers of cotton textile as the substrate material, with the conductive coating paint used on the radiating element and the groundplane. The radiating element is formed into a disc shape comprises four patches and fed by an open ring feeding network with a circumference of around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>. Each patch segment is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> phase-shifted to achieve different phase of wave radiation utilizable to gain circular polarization. The characterization results show that the array antenna resonates at the frequency of 5.8 GHz with the bandwidth response of 270 MHz, making it suitable for WBAN communications.

articleTitle: Explaining the Identification of Granular Crack with Deep Learning and XAI
abstract: Precise detection of granular fractures is crucial for various engineering applications, and Deep Learning approaches can transform imaging methodologies and material analysis. This study employed a convolutional neural network (CNN) that incorporated explainability elements to improve the trustworthiness and transparency of the model in classifying granular cracks. After conducting thorough model comparisons and analyses, a bespoke model was chosen. Extensive model comparisons and analyses led to the selection of a custom model with 91% training accuracy and optimized parameters. Fine-tuning of six pre-trained models identified VGG-16 as the top performer, achieving 99.96% training accuracy and 97.7% testing accuracy. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, particularly the insertion method, provided robust interpretability, with attributed scores of 0.96 for insertion, 0.69 for deletion, and 0.37 for fidelity. Visualization using various attribution mapping methods reinforced the trustworthiness of this work in granular crack identification.

articleTitle: Channel Capacity Enhancement in Dual Branch MRC under Extreme Fading Using Quantum Computing
abstract: We have investigated the potential of channel capacity and signal integrity enhancement in dual branch MRC systems even under extreme fading through classical and quantum computing. We have used the classical algorithm to gauge the performance of the quantum algorithm, including QAOA and QEC. Our simulation results show that quantum-assisted MRC work optimally by providing superior SNR and BER. Quantum algorithms not only maximizes the effective channel capacity but also minimizes end-to-end system latency and number of error rate more efficiently. The addition of Quantum Machine Learning for the dynamic parameter setting in real-time has demonstrated that it may be possible to combat severe fading effects. To the best of our knowledge, this paper laid the cornerstone to explore more opportunities in implementing quantum-enabled techniques for advanced telecommunication system development to realize more robust and efficient technologies.

articleTitle: Virtual Inertia Emulation in Standalone Microgrid with Photovoltaic-Battery Energy Storage System
abstract: Power generation from large-scale renewable energy sources like photovoltaics (PV) reduces the inertia and damping characteristics of the power system, leading to oscillations. In a standalone microgrid PV-Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), control is achieved using a Dual-Loop Virtual Synchronous Generator (DLVSG) control. This control mechanism provides virtual inertia and virtual damping to support frequency and voltage stability. This paper proposes a control strategy that imitates the rotational inertia and damping characteristics of synchronous generators based on the VSG operating principle. Adopting this control approach has emerged as a promising solution for enhancing the integration of renewable energy sources into microgrids. The proposed standalone microgrid with PV-BESS employs the Perturb and Observe Maximum Power Point Tracking (P&O MPPT) technique to achieve maximum power extraction and includes a bidirectional converter for the BESS. Simulation results demonstrate that the DLVSG control improves grid stability, power quality, robustness, and the ability to handle perturbations.

articleTitle: Experimental Approaches on Properties Characterization of Magneto-Dielectric Material Using SIW Structure
abstract: This paper discusses experimental approaches on properties characterization of magneto-dielectric (MD) material using Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) structure. The characterized MD material takes a cylindrical shape of Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG), while the properties to be characterized is focused on the material permittivity. Two SIW structures are designed and fabricated for the properties characterization, namely SIW structure with host material using FR-4 Epoxy substrate and without host material or air-host SIW structure. In the middle of SIW structure with host, a cylindrical hole with the diameter of 18.1 mm and the height of 4.8 mm is provided for placing MD material to be characterized. Based on experimental characterization, the SIW structure with host has a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode cut-off frequency of 2.05 GHz, while a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode cut-off frequency for the air-host SIW structure is 3.85 GHz. In addition, the result of properties characterization achieves an accuracy of 96.99%.

articleTitle: Equivalent Meandered-Straight Line Concept and Its Implementation for Device Miniaturization
abstract: This paper presents an equivalent meandered-straight line concept for miniaturizing microwave devices. To demonstrate the concept, a rectangular meander line model was developed based on theoretical approach. The developed model is applied to design a meandered line, which is equivalent to a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35-\Omega$</tex> straight line. Good agreement in simulated and measured responses between the meandered-straight line and the corresponding one confirms the proposed concept. The designed meandered line is then implemented to miniaturize a hybrid coupler. The miniaturized hybrid coupler occupies an area of 0.73 times than of the conventional footprint and exhibits good performance. The average transmission amplitude is -3.42 dB, with a very small amplitude imbalance of ±0.05 dB. Moreover, the measured bandwidth for -10 dB reflection coefficient is 830 MHz (34.58%), which indicates a wideband characteristic response.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of Axial-Mode Bifilar Helix-Conical Antenna for ISM Band Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the design and realization of an axial-mode bifilar helix-conical antenna is proposed for 2.4 GHz ISM bands wireless communications. The proposed bifilar helix-conical antenna is made by two copper conductor wires with the diameter of 0.5 mm and fed by a 50–Ω SubMiniature version A (SMA) connector through a microstrip line deployed on a Flame Retardant (FR) 4 Epoxy dielectric substrate. The copper conductor wires are turning twice for attaining axial-mode of radiation pattern and yielding a conical shape by varying the diameter with a certain radius change. The design of bifilar helix-conical antenna is optimized and characterized to attain an optimum configuration. Some basic parameters such as resonant frequency, bandwidth response, and radiation pattern are used to evaluate the radiation characteristics of proposed antenna. The characterization result shows that the proposed bifilar helix-conical antenna can work at the operating frequency of 2.4 GHz with the bandwidth response of 200 MHz and the axial-mode of radiation pattern.

articleTitle: 3.5 GHz Reflective Electromagnetic Surfaces for Linear-to-Circular Polarizer
abstract: Manipulating the polarization of electromagnetic waves is crucial for maximizing receiving power and capacity in communication systems. This paper presents a straightforward structure and method for a Reflective Electromagnetic Surface (RES) to achieve the conversion of polarization from linearly polarized incident waves to circularly polarized reflected waves. The unit cell structure of this polarizer features a square patch incorporated with a rectangular slot oriented at 45-degrees in the center of patch. Simulation results show that the incorporation of a rectangular slot with a 45-degree orientation in the center of patch produces an axial ratio of less than 3 dB at the frequency of 3.5 GHz, demonstrating its capability to produce circularly polarized reflected wave. Prototyping of proposed RES for Linear-to-Circular (LTC) polarizer, consisting of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\times 6$</tex> square patches, is deployed on a 210 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 210$</tex> mm printed circuit board. Measurements of manufactured prototype show that co- and cross-polarizations of reflection coefficient value are similar to the simulation. Therefore, it can be concluded that the proposed RES structure can function effectively as an LTC polarizer.

articleTitle: A GIS Based Study on Solar Thermal System Integration for Domestic Hot Water Needs
abstract: This paper aims to provide a good concept of installing solar collectors by considering different aspects such as collector parameters, efficiency, sizing, energy demand etc. Promatop 1.5 (vertical) collector model has been chosen for the solar thermal system integration with a view to considering Domestic Hot Water (DHW) usage. Besides, Spanish CTE regulation on different aspects has also been considered for this work. Utilizing the Photovoltaic Geographical Information System (PVGIS) open-source interactive tool for collecting solar related data is also a good aspect of this study. Further, this study provides a compact overview of the integration of solar thermal systems to understand its main characteristics and requirements.

articleTitle: Split Topology Based 8-Bit Flash ADC Architecture for Reduced Conversion Time
abstract: This paper presents the design of 8-bit flash ADC architecture using split based technique. The proposed design requires only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2(2^{N/ 2}-1)$</tex> number of comparators for N-bit of resolution and occupies only 30 comparators for 8-bit flash ADC instead of 255 comparators. The proposed architecture has resulted in less number of comparators due to split topology and incorporating intermediate stage in between. The ADC is designed on UMC 180nm CMOS technology and obtains the conversion time and power dissipation of only 3.46ns and 110mW respectively at 1.8V power supply.

articleTitle: Innovative Non-Isolated DC-DC Converter Design with High Gain and Reduced Switch Voltage Stress for DC Microgrid Applications
abstract: DC microgrids have become increasingly significant due to the effective integration of renewable energy sources such as fuel cells and photovoltaics (PV) through power electronic interfaces. This integration allows for a more sustainable and efficient energy system by harnessing the potential of renewable sources. However, one of the critical challenges in this process is the lower voltage levels at which these renewable energy sources operate. To address this issue, DC-DC converters play a crucial role. These converters are essential for stepping up or down the voltage levels to match the requirements of the DC microgrid, ensuring seamless and efficient connectivity. As a result, the deployment of DC-DC converters not only facilitates the incorporation of renewable energy into the grid but also enhances the overall stability and performance of the DC micro-grid system. This paper presents an innovative dual-switch, ultra-high gain, non-isolated DC-DC converter with low voltage stress. By combining a modified switched inductor (SI) and a switched capacitor (SC) and replacing the diode in the SI cell with an additional switch, the converter achieves significant voltage gain and reduces voltage stress on active switches to less than 25% of the output voltage. Experimental results from a 380V, 200W prototype show a full-load efficiency of 95.79% and excellent component utilization.

articleTitle: Design and Performance of an On-Board/On-Road Electric Rickshaw PV Roof-Top Battery Charger
abstract: Popularity of electric rickshaw (e-Rickshaw) is gaining manifold in semi-developed countries for providing ease of first and last mile public transportation without any environment challenging pollution threat. But to make more cycles and from last destination battery charge condition is still a big challenge for e-Rickshaw's owners. To overcome this issue “an on-road/on-board e-rickshaw battery charger is designed”, to keep the battery charge condition at near to nominal, at least during day time through mounting a single 500W photovoltaic (PV) solar panel at its roof-top with a coupled inductor based buck-boost single-ended primary inductance converter (SEPIC) to reduce the weight and cost, and to increase the efficiency and over all power density with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm for on-road charging even while driving. Other benefits of on-road charging are that, battery's charge-discharge cycle is reduced hence life is increased. Moreover, battery never goes into deep discharge. A hardware prototype is developed with Microchip DSPIC microcontroller with MOSFETs and Schottky diodes.

articleTitle: Modelling and Control of Microgrids in an Offgrid Operating Scenario: A Case Study
abstract: A system comprising of distributed energy resources, batteries, loads which are integrated and controlled like a single entity with confined electrical boundaries, often termed as microgrid, may operate in either grid tied or offgrid mode and provides efficient and flexible power flow. This feature ensures timely and effective response to load deviations and dispersed generating output, while maintaining stability and performance. Microgrid control solutions must be robust enough to run alongside and independently from the utility grid while maintaining power quality standards. The paper proposes a model of network forming inverter feeding a local load and operating independently of utility grid and its associated primary controls. Droop control, a well-known and easy-to model approach, is used to modify the frequency and voltage magnitude in relation to active and reactive power signals. A discretized SVM (space vector modulation) technique is utilized to convert modulating signals into pulses to drive the power electronics based inverter. Computer simulations on MATLAB Simulink software are performed to evaluate the efficacy of these approaches.

articleTitle: An Efficient sEMG Signal Acquisition System for Decoding of Hand Movements
abstract: A pattern recognition system based on human movements or electromyography signals comprises various stages, from signal acquisition to control. The primary signal acquisition stage is the most important since the further stages largely depend on the quality of recorded signals. This work proposes an NI ELVIS-based signal acquisition system for recording human muscle movement signals. To capture muscle signals, NI ELVIS board is integrated with a BioAmp-EMG biopotential amplifier module. Six distinct hand movements for five subjects are recorded to evaluate the proposed hardware setup. The obtained signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for different measurements is above 10 dB, and the average of the SNR values is approximately 16.44 dB, which signifies the high noise immunity of the proposed hardware. The SNR is also compared with the state of the art available sEMG acquisition modules. Further, eight time-domain features, including a novel feature, have been extracted to train Linear discriminant Analysis (LDA), Decision Tree (DT), and Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers for a pattern recognition-based movement decoding application. The testing results show an average accuracy of 91.01 % for LDA, 83.82 % for DT, and 80.29 % for MLP classifiers.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach to Predict Ratings for Book Recommendation System Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: A recommender system is a tool that suggests products or services to users based on their preferences and past behavior, enhancing user satisfaction and engagement. Accurate rating prediction is crucial as it directly impacts the system's ability to provide relevant and personalized recommendations, thereby improving the overall user experience. In this study, we introduce an innovative approach to recommendation systems by proposing an Weighted Hybrid Model that combines an Adaptive K-Nearest Neighbors (AKNN) algorithm and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). The AKNN algorithm dynamically adjusts the number of neighbors based on user rating density, providing a tailored neighborhood size for each user. By incorporating a hybrid similarity measure that combines cosine similarity, Pearson correlation, and Variance Mean Difference (VMD), our AKNN algorithm effectively captures the multifaceted nature of user-item relationships. We further enhance our recommendation model by combining AKNN with SVD through optimized weighting, creating a Weighted Hybrid Model. This model balances the contributions of the AKNN and SVD components, leveraging the strengths of both approaches to minimize prediction errors. Our evaluation results demonstrate that the Weighted Hybrid Model outperforms several algorithms, including standalone KNN with Z-Score, Item-wise Variance-Mean based Recommender System (IVMRS), KNN with RJAC DUB, and Pearson Baseline with Weighted KNN. The Weighted Hybrid Model achieved the lowest Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.54491 and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.17839, indicating superior predictive accuracy.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Differential Voltage and Sense Amplifier Offset on Power and Delay of SRAM in 65nm LSTP Technology
abstract: Sense amplifier is a circuit that helps in the reading operation of the data stored in a memory array. In this paper, we have investigated the trade-off between the differential voltage on bit lines provided at the input of the sense amplifier with respect to the power and delay of the memory array. We observe that there is a decrease in the power of the memory array by 27.40%, 24.18%, and 17.33% for array configurations with 32, 64, and 128 rows, respectively if we increase the differential voltage of bit-lines provided to the sense amplifier. We also observe a decrease in delay by 23.70% and 14.20% with 32 and 64 rows, respectively. This technique is useful for applications with fewer rows in a memory array. The analysis is performed on input decoupled latch type sense amplifier for array configurations with 32,64,128,256 and 512 rows at 65 nm LSTP technology.

articleTitle: Tidal Energy Assessment of River Karnaphuli: A Technical Analysis
abstract: Most of the power generation in Bangladesh is gas-based and approximately 92% is based on fossil fuel which is a major problem for this country. Consequently, the government is searching for alternate energy sources, particularly renewable energy. In recent years solar energy has become popular by the government and people's support. Despite having a huge potential for tidal energy, there is no such step to harness it yet. This paper mainly focuses on the tidal energy potential of the Karnaphuli River and proposes a tidal barrage for Khal No-18. Being the most potent location of river Karnaphuli for tidal power in terms of tidal height, there has been no substantial work available for this location. The main focus of the study is tidal range variation, mean potential energy, approximate peak and lowest potential in every month of a year, and estimation of annual power output by tidal energy from the location Khal no 18. At the same time, this study contains a proposal for a tidal barrage with turbine numbers and also suggests for higher efficiency of power generation.

articleTitle: Simulation of ECG Signals Using Coupled Aliev-Panfilov Oscillators
abstract: Computer models for ECG simulation are very useful for testing computerized ECG interpretation software and systems and for educational purposes. This work considers the recently proposed oscillatory type of the Aliev-Panfilov equation instead of the modified Van der Pol equation as the pacemaking element for a coupled three-oscillator cardiac conduction system model. We simulated ECGs of several typical arrhythmias and compared the results obtained with both model variants. By changing the pacemaker model, we expanded the capabilities of the cardiac conduction system model without changing its structure. This modification allowed us to reproduce some cardiac arrhythmias more accurately and simulate additional cardiac phenomena, such as junctional rhythms, demonstrating the advantages of using the Aliev-Panfilov equation in the model.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Rail Monitoring System for 1:3 Laboratory Train Using Fiber Bragg Grating Sensors
abstract: Development of railway networks depends on continuous structural and operation monitoring of train and its parts in real time. This paper describes the condition monitoring of train wheels and rail by using fiber optic sensors. A new 1:3 downscale test train is developed to study the rail-wheel interactions. Two laboratory experiments were carried out in the test train using fiber Bragg grating as strain sensors. First is the wagon load analysis, followed by flat wheel detection. A good agreement of results is observed with sensitivity of sensor 1.31pm /µε and reflectivity of 89.51%. By applying proper filtering techniques, we can observe the high frequency dynamic vibrations in the rail wheel system.

articleTitle: Design of O+E Band Hybrid Optical Signal Amplifier via Praseodymium and Thulium Doped Fibers
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid optical amplifier (HOA) for O+eband amplification is presented using a Praseodymium-doped fiber amplifier (PDFA) and Thulium-doped fiber amplifier (TDFA) by optimizing the pumping schemes and amplifiers' lengths. A signal gain (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>)> 15.03 dB and noise figure (NF)< 5.2 dB with a maximum gain of 46.56 dB at 1310 nm have been observed for the wavelength region of 1280 nm to 1470 nm. Also, the gain maximizes to values> 30 dB in the wavelength ranges of 1290 nm to 1350 nm and 1420 nm to 1470 nm. The impact of the nonlinear ion-ion interaction mechanism (IM) effect on the signal gain is also observed and minimized by optimizing the amplifier's parameters. Utilizing the optimized set of parameters in the O-band, a gain deterioration of 1.93% has been observed at the wavelength of 1310 nm. Apparently, in the E band, the gain increases to 0.3% at the wavelength of 1390 nm with the inclusion of IM effects.

articleTitle: Cloud Server Enabled IoT Integrated Smart Wrist Band for Women's Protection Remotely
abstract: This work proposes an IoT framework that incorporates a smart wearable wristband for the protection of girls and women using a cloud server from a remote location. This can be embedded into a wrist that is easy to wear, easy to carry, and easy to operate. It consists of 3 sensor units including a pulse oxy meter, pressure sensor, and sound detector. When any stranger attacks a woman or girl by means of holding her hand, the pressure sensor will activate the device. Even if the stranger doesn't hold the hand, the device will be activated by a pulse oximeter sensor. This sensor is continuously monitoring her pulse rate and SpO2, and when the value exceeds the reset value, the device will be activated and it will send the data to the cloud through the Wi-Fi module to send the data to the victim's home without any delay. The performance of the proposed technology has been evaluated in terms of output from sensors along with the ThingSpeak IoT server.

articleTitle: Secure and Resilient Threat Modelling Strategy for Drone Delivery System
abstract: Several unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are used in multi-drone delivery systems to move packages and supplies from a distribution center to specific delivery locations. The key challenges in multi-drone delivery are navigating complex aviation, reliable performance, protection of drones from hacking, ensuring the security of deliveries, gaining public trust, and maintaining privacy. This paper suggests an approach to develop the secured and authentic data structure of drone delivery systems. The paper presents the common threat actors, and identifies different stages of possible threats in drone delivery. The various threat modeling tools are mentioned. This paper proposes the DSA (digital signature algorithm) based secure and resilient algorithm for drone-delivery systems.

articleTitle: Predictive Insights: Empowering Early Detection of Lung Cancer Using Machine Learning Excellence
abstract: Recognition and prediction of lung cancer at the earliest possible stage can significantly increase patient survival. But it is challenging to identify lung cancer's early symptoms and predict cancer-based on them. This paper implements a machine learning algorithm to predict lung cancer by using the most correlated symptoms of lung cancer. By applying data visualization and feature extraction techniques, we found the most correlated symptoms of lung cancer and predicted them using logistic regression, support vector machine, and k nearest neighbor classifiers; among them, support vector machine and logistic regression both showed higher accuracy in lung cancer detection, with 98.52 % accuracy in the training set and 98.39 % accuracy in the testing set.

articleTitle: BlissBot: Mental Health Chatbot
abstract: “Blissbot” is an innovative and interactive chatbot project designed to address the critical need for accessible mental health education. This project aims to create a user-friendly chatbot platform that serves as a virtual mental health educator, providing essential information, resources, and support to individuals seeking guidance and knowledge about mental health. The chatbot employs natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning algorithms to enhance its conversational abilities, ensuring a more human-like interaction and understanding of users' emotional states. Furthermore, it prioritizes user privacy and data security, adhering to strict confidentiality measures. The project's impact is far-reaching, aiming to break down barriers to mental health education by providing a scalable, 24/7 accessible platform. By empowering individuals with accurate information and supportive resources, “EmpowerMinds” strives to reduce stigma, increase mental health literacy, and promote proactive self-care practices, ultimately contributing to improved overall well-being in society.

articleTitle: Laser-Induced Graphene-Based Flexible Strain Sensor for Human Finger Motion Detection
abstract: Wearable and flexible electronic devices are important in health monitoring systems. Laser-induced graphene (LIG) has gained popularity in flexible electronics due to its distinct physical and electrical properties. LIG can be formed by direct irradiation of the laser on polyimide (PI) film, resulting in a porous structure with high conductivity. In this study, resistive laser-induced graphene sensors of three different shapes with similar surface areas were engraved on the PI film. The response of resistive strain sensors was measured in terms of resistance by bending them at various angles ranging from 0 to 90 degrees. The performance of the three different sensors with the same surface area of 130 mm2 was compared and its reversibility and repeatability were investigated. The developed resistive LIG strain sensor provides a stable and fast response with high sensitivity.

articleTitle: Assessment of Antenna Polarization Effect on Radiated Emissions Measurement
abstract: Antennas with reconfigurable polarization capability are useful to diminish losses affected by multi path fading, thereby enhancing the efficiency of transceived signals. This is undertaken by minimizing disparities in antenna polarization and signal interference with others. This paper assesses the effect of antenna polarization on radiated emissions measurement of equipment under test (EUT). The measurements are conducted at an EMI test system using microstrip antenna in the frequency range of 30 MHz to 1000MHz. As comparison, the measurement using an Ultralog antenna is also performed in the same frequency range. The used microstrip antenna is designed to work with different polarization modes, specifically linear polarization (LP), left hand circular polarization (LHCP), right hand circular polarization (RHCP). From the measurement results, the electric field strength levels in vertical polarization are higher than that in horizontal polarization for all polarization modes of microstrip antennas. The varying level of electric field strength in vertical polarization is in the ranges of 85.59 dBμV/m to 86.91 dBμV/m, while in horizontal polarization mode is 70.70 dBμV/m to 80.42 dBμV/m.

articleTitle: Leveraging XAI and Breakthrough Machine Learning Techniques for Trigeminal Neuralgia Severity Classification
abstract: Trigeminal Neuralgia (TN) is a debilitating chronic pain disorder that significantly diminishes overall well-being, making diagnosis and therapy more challenging. The quick and precise categorization of TN severity is critical to therapy effectiveness. To assess the severity of TN, this study makes use of advanced machine learning techniques and explainable AI (XAI) approaches. We use a range of bagging and boosting strategies, including AdaBoost, Random Forest, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Gradient Boosting, and Logistic Regression. Random Forest was 95.2% accurate, whereas AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting were 92% and 97.2% in terms of their accuracy. The Decision Tree classifier obtained an accuracy of 84.62%, while K-Nearest Neighbours and Logistic Regression also achieved 92.31% accuracy. F1- score, precision, and recall metrics were used to assess performance on a dataset that included patient demographics and medical histories. XAI techniques, such as LIME and SHAP values, were used to improve the models' readability and transparency, which helped to progress the creation of cutting-edge diagnostic tools and increase clinician and researcher confidence.

articleTitle: A Power-Efficient Core Micro-Architecture Based on RISC-V Instruction Set Architecture
abstract: RISC processors have become a dominant force in processor design due to their simplicity and efficiency. One such architecture, RISC-V, offers a powerful yet streamlined instruction set, making it a popular choice for embedded systems. This paper delves into the design of a RISC processor with a particular focus on optimizing the power consumption of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Since multipliers are known to be the most power-hungry components within an ALU, the paper proposes a redesign of the multiplier's internal circuitry using suitable alternatives. Specifically, the design utilizes the Baugh-Wooley algorithm for signed multiplication due to its efficiency. Furthermore, the paper details how the internal circuit of this multiplier is redesigned to minimize both power consumption and area footprint, ultimately leading to a more energy-efficient system overall. By focusing on optimizing the power-hungry multiplier within the ALU, this design approach aims to reduce the overall power consumption of the RISC-V processor significantly. The proposed system is implemented in Verilog HDL. The proposed design optimizes the area and power by reducing 18.5% and 7.4% respectively when compared to the existing system.

articleTitle: Evaluating Neural Network Parameter Obliteration in Catastrophic Forgetting
abstract: One of the major weaknesses of Neural Networks is their inability to learn multiple functions (tasks) sequentially. This phenomenon is observed when a data distribution shift is encountered in continual learning, leading to catastrophic forgetting. Such ability is foremost important to develop models with general intelligence. In this paper, we evaluate how different parts of the neural network contribute to overall forgetting by investigating the training dynamics during different methods of continual learning. We evaluate and analyze the learning dynamics in catastrophic forgetting on frequently used classification models on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST datasets. Our findings reveal a consistent trend in continual learning scenarios, both in domain-incremental and class-incremental settings. Specifically, gamma means demonstrate stability in earlier layers but exhibit increased plasticity in later layers, indicating heightened adaptability to changes in data distributions.

articleTitle: Towards Robust Pneumonia Detection: An Ensemble Model Approach
abstract: Pneumonia is a respiratory illness that is particularly dangerous to children under the age of five, accounting for a high percentage of deaths in this group. With the advent of new technologies such as deep learning, researchers are optimistic about the potential to utilize these techniques for accurately distinguishing between normal and pneumonia-afflicted X-ray images. This paper tackles the problem of pneumonia detection by using a deep learning approach that incorporates Transfer Learning and an ensemble model, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 96.31%. The methodology leverages three primary models—MobileNet, MobileNetV2, and DenseNet169. The resulting model surpasses the performance of several established models, effectively striking a balance in accurately discerning between normal lung images and those indicative of infection. The recommended method has the potential to improve pneumonia diagnosis accuracy while saving clinicians a significant amount of time.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of Blockchain Based Triple Branch MRC for Secured Communication in Adverse Fading Conditions
abstract: The investigation in this study entails integrating blockchain technology with maximal ratio combining in a triple branch configuration for secure communications under multipath fading conditions. The proposed combines blockchain's decentralized and immutable characteristics with MRC's communication outcomes and flaws, which are worsened by the multipath fading channels. To evaluate this, the team carried out various empirical tests with the key findings being the Signal-to-Noise Ratio performance. Since the blockchain integrated system is anticipated to exhibit a higher SNR, our results showed a substantial increase in SNR. This confirms the robust and secure communication capabilities of the integrated solution under study. Therefore, the researchers demonstrate how blockchain can greatly enhance security as well as the quality of the communication, presenting a better solution in challenging data transmission conditions. This study establishes the foundation for further research on blockchain technology applications in the communication field.

articleTitle: Lightweight Deep Multiscale Feature Learning for Improved Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) is a significant field within human-computer interaction, often utilizing deep learning (DL) techniques for improved performance. However, DL's resource-intensive nature poses challenges, especially on memory-limited devices like smartphones and other edge devices. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach combining Wavelet Transform (WT) and DL. By decomposing smartphone signals using WT and feeding them into a Multiscale Con-volutional Neural Network (MSCNN), our method effectively extracts features at different scales for adaptive HAR without the need for manual feature extraction. This WT-MSCNN model offers advantages in processing non-stationary data, extracting HAR information effectively, and maintaining robustness to scale uncertainties in signals. Our experimental results indicate that the proposed methodology attains an accuracy of 98 %, a sensitivity of 99%, a specificity of 97%, and an Fl-score of 98.10% on NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU (Graphics Processing Unit). Additionally, our model has demonstrated enhanced throughput, outperforming fine-tuned MobileNet-V3 and SqueezeNet Models by 83.59% and 25.72% respectively on the Raspberry Pi 4 hardware platform.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of QBQ-Copter: A Novel Morphing Drone
abstract: This paper introduces a novel shape-changing Quad-copter with a tilt mechanism. The proposed drone mechanism consists of two main arms. The bottom arm serves as the body frame and the top arm is allowed to rotate about the bottom arm along one axis. Tiltable propellers are employed for the top arm. The drone can be operated as a conventional Quadcopter. During maneuvers in tight spaces, it can be operated as a Bi-Quadcopter which is a Bicopter with the auxiliary thrust-tilting mechanism. The morphology-dependent dynamic control allocation is carefully designed. A nonlinear position controller is implemented with the double loop cascaded attitude control approach. The position control performance of the proposed drone is verified through the simulations.

articleTitle: Enhanced Bidirectional DC/DC Converter Utilizing Fuzzy-PI Control with PWM for Dual-Battery Hybrid Electric Vehicles
abstract: The purpose of this research is to present an improved bidirectional DC/DC converter for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), which incorporates a dual-battery energy storage system. When it comes to switching pulse production, traditional methods frequently make use of pulse-width modulation (PWM) that is based on proportional-integral (PI) modulation. Although this method is effective, it can result in problems with noise and variations in output. In order to overcome these obstacles, we offer a novel control technique that blends fuzzy logic with PI control (also known as fuzzy PI) in conjunction with pulse width modulation (PWM). The purpose of this procedure is to enhance the performance of the converter by significantly lowering the levels of noise and smoothing out the features of the output. Through comparative research, it has been demonstrated that the Fuzzy PI technique greatly improves system stability and response under a variety of load conditions, hence providing a more robust solution for the management of HEV energy production. It is possible that the deployment of this advanced control technique would result in battery electric vehicle (HEV) systems that are more efficient and dependable, thereby contributing to the growth of automotive technology.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Self Testable Fast Multiplier Architecture
abstract: Multiplication operations play a fundamental role in numerous digital applications, and guaranteeing their accuracy is imperative for reliable system performance. The research carried out in this paper entails two primary aspects. Initially, an 8x8 unsigned fast multiplier is developed which is a modified Wallace tree multiplier. The choice of employing a Wallace tree multiplier is motivated by its ability to minimize latency. Additionally, to further boost the speed of the Wallace tree multiplier, a Kogge Stone adder module is incorporated. Further, a Built-In Self -Test (BIST) module is designed for the modified Wallace tree multiplier. The efficacy of the BIST is evaluated by considering Stuck at fault model, ensuring thorough test coverage. The BIST mechanism is customized to identify stuck-at faults within the multiplier module.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Malware Detection in Cloud Portable Executable Files
abstract: A major cybersecurity threat is posed by malicious software, which is constantly changing. These novel threats are difficult for traditional signature-based detection techniques to identify. By identifying novel patterns, machine learning (ML) frameworks can enhance malware detection. This study examines malware detection using machine learning techniques with an emphasis on characteristics found in cloud Portable Executable (PE) headers. It examines several machine learning approaches, such as random forest, logistic regression, and artificial neural networks (ANN). The outcomes demonstrate the value of feature selection and algorithm tuning for high detection rates, empha- sizing machine learning's effectiveness in malware detection.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Deep Neural Features for Classification of Gait Abnormality
abstract: Clinical gait analysis plays a vital role in diagnosis and monitoring neurological and musculoskeletal injuries. Quali-tative gait assessment depends on subjective observations, manual measurements, and specialized equipment. Recently machine learning and deep learning based models have demonstrated sig-nificant accuracy in gait analysis. But dynamic feature extraction is always a challenging problem in temporal gait data analysis. After extracting dynamic features, a Fully-connected Neural Network (FNN) is employed to classify of gait abnormalities using GaitRec standard dataset. The proposed multi-modal features based classification model achieves 96.22 % accuracy and it outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: DC Link Voltage Balance and Discharge in Three-Level NPC Fed PMSM-Powered EVs Using External Circuit
abstract: The paper introduces a voltage balance control algorithm designed to balance and discharge the DC link voltage in three-level neutral-point clamped (NPC) multilevel inverters feeding to permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) based Electric Vehicle (EV). The paper also describes the DC bus voltage discharge on account of the emergency condition due to safety reasons. The control logic is implemented with the use of space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) to balance the DC link capacitors of the NPC with the help of an external circuit. In this method the NPC feeding to the PMSM operate normally with balanced dc link voltages. At a moment when suddenly the load increases or due to any emergence condition the DC link voltage gets unbalanced, then at this time the external circuit will get activated. The control logic will adjust the operation of the switches in such a way to keep the DC link in a minimum band of variations to provide system stability and balance the dc bus voltages. The scheme is performed on MATLAB simulations to verify the results in transients and emergent conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Input Parallel Output Series Full Bridge Converter Considering Parasitic Effects
abstract: The Input Parallel Output Series (IPOS) Full-Bridge DC-DC converter offers significant advantages over the conventional Full-Bridge converter by connecting multiple modules in parallel on the input side and in series on the output side. This configuration enhances voltage gain, improves overall efficiency, reliability, and scalability. MATLAB simulations are carried out to demonstrate the IPOS converter's superior performance in terms of voltage output and efficiency. Additionally, the IPOS design provides enhanced redundancy; if one module fails, the others continue to operate, ensuring uninterrupted performance. This makes the IPOS Full-Bridge converter ideal for applications in renewable energy systems, electric vehicles, and other high-performance power management scenarios.

Author Keywords: Input Parallel Output Series (IPOS) Full-Bridge converter

articleTitle: A Multi-Modal Contrastive Learning Framework for Identifying Similar Patients with Cervical Dysplasia from Unlabeled Colposcopy Data
abstract: Cervical dysplasia, a precancerous condition of the cervix, can progress to cervical cancer if left untreated, making its early identification crucial. The proposed framework utilizes a multi-modal contrastive learning approach to identify similar patients of cervical dysplasia by combining textual doctor's prescriptions and colposcopic images. This novel method stands out by leveraging contrastive learning with multi-modal data, which is effective in scenarios with limited labeled data. The framework integrates deep learning techniques to extract complex features from colposcopic data as well as patients' textual report through utilizing unimodal text and image encoders as base encoders. Then a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based Variational auto encoder (VAE) is added to extract salient features. Modality fusion is achieved by using separate encoders for image and text representation generation, followed by concatenating these representations for training in the multi-modal vector space using a contrastive learning approach. The experimental plan involves data preparation, model training, and inference to identify similar patients with cervical dysplasia. The model aims to capture optimal latent embeddings to identify similar patients accurately from unlabeled dataset. Therefore, by extracting meaningful representations from the combined data modalities, the framework aims to find the similar patients in cervical dysplasia, offering a novel and potentially impactful avenue for healthcare analytics.

articleTitle: Integration of Various ROS Packages for Autonomous Navigation and Mapping of Mobile Robot
abstract: The integration of the Robot Operating System (ROS) into navigation and mapping strategies has significantly advanced autonomous systems. This study explores the implementation of autonomous navigation and mapping techniques using ROS, focusing on the integration of sensor data, such as LiDAR, for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). This enables robots to navigate unknown environments while constructing accurate maps in real-time. The work integrates various ROS packages and algorithms, first in virtual simulation and then in a physical robot. Through a series of experiments and simulations, the study demonstrates the effectiveness of ROS in achieving precise navigation and mapping outcomes, providing valuable insights for the advancement of autonomous robotic platforms.

articleTitle: Exploring Gene Regulatory Networks and Identification of Therapeutic Targets and Potential Drugs with Diseases among PSP, nfvPPA and AD
abstract: Bioinformatics conceptualizes biological processes to obtain information from biological data in terms of genomics. Background research demonstrates that Progressive supranu-clear palsy (PSP), nonfluent variant primary progressive aphasia (nfvPPA), and Alzheimer's disease (AD) share a significant number of biochemical and genetic characteristics. To conduct this study, we collect GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus), datasets from NCBI. The goal of our research are to identify commonly shared differentially expressed genes (DEGs), PPI network, hub genes, higher degree interactions of micro-RNAs and transcriptional factors from gene regulatory networks(GRN), functional assessment with gene ontology for identifying significant biological functions and signaling pathways for therapeutic targets among PSP, nfvPPA, and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Additionally, this research aims to provide insights for drug design by exploring gene regulatory networks, and protein-drug interactions, contributing to the development of effective treatments.

articleTitle: A Segmented Hybrid CAM for High Speed Application Using FinFET
abstract: This work presents a high-speed, power-efficient content addressable memory (CAM) that enables parallel lookups for fast matching with minimal power impact. The design introduces three key innovations firstly pre-charge free operation, which eliminates additional node charging time, enhancing search speed and reducing power consumption; secondly a Hybrid Match Line (HML) structure that balances power and delay by combining the high speed of NOR and low power of NAND; and finally a local searching technique that further reduces search time. These innovations collectively improve performance significantly. Implemented using 20 nm FinFET technology for a 1 × 32 memory array. Compared to the best existing designs, this CAM shows a 87% speed improvement and a 88% better energy, and 96% improvement in Energy- delay product(EDP).

articleTitle: Electro-Mechanical Design Analysis and Implementation of an Indigenous Mars Rover
abstract: This paper presents the results of an ongoing research project titled ‘Rover-71’, which focuses on the design and development of an indigenous Mars Rover. The primary goal of this research is to build the Rover that can survive the harsh environment on Mars and also for educational purpose for general understanding. It was planned in such a way that it could run autonomously and also be controlled via a wireless system. This extensive project is subdivided into several stages, and this paper is the outcome of the first portion of the project, where the mechanical and electrical systems were built in an innovative and indigenous way. The results were proven through rigorous simulation, and the optimal design was implemented while taking into account the availability of the components in the local market. The structure was built in the workshop using the blueprint generated by the SolidWorks simulation software. The outcome was successful, as the Rover-71 functioned properly with the ability to collect various data from the surroundings.

articleTitle: Ensemble-Based Botnet Attack Detection and Classification Using Machine Learning Algorithms on NBaIoT Dataset
abstract: Through botnet assaults, Mirai and BASHLITE present serious risks in the context of the Internet of Things (loT). A reliable detection and classification model is the need of the hour. This article presents a solution to the problem by suggesting an ensemble-based algorithm to detect and classify different categories of Mirai and BASHLITE attacks. We have used the NBaloT, a heterogeneous dataset, that purposefully com-promised on many devices, and exposes subtle attack categories. Interestingly, certain devices resist Mirai infections, improving our analysis. By utilizing important data types and various time-based window sizes, our approach seeks to create an effective model for identifying and classifying IoT botnet assaults to strengthen the IoT ecosystem against new attacks.

articleTitle: Human Mental State Detection Using Modified Convolutional Neural Network with Leaky Rectified Linear Unit
abstract: In the present investigation, we explored the application of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for classifying human mental states based on responses to questions related to mental health. The dataset includes responses aimed at evaluating various mental health conditions, providing a comprehensive basis for analysis. Our proposed CNNs architecture features multiple convolutional and pooling layers, followed by dense layers with leaky rectified linear unit (ReLU) activations to capture intricate patterns in the data. To prevent overfitting and ensure robust generalization, we integrate ridge regression (L2) regularization and dropout techniques during training. The model is optimized using the Adam optimizer and a binary cross-entropy loss function, striking a balance between computational efficiency and model performance. We evaluate the model's performance using standard metrics, including accuracy, confusion matrix, and classification report, achieving a notable accuracy of 90.24% on validation data. To gain deeper insights into the model's effectiveness, we employ receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and precision-recall curves, which illustrate the model's proficiency in identifying individuals with mental disorders while minimizing false positives and false negatives. Our findings highlight the significant potential of CNNs in mental health classification tasks, demonstrating substantial accuracy and generalization. This model represents a promising tool for the early detection and intervention of mental health disorders, potentially transforming healthcare outcomes and enhancing the quality of life for affected individuals. By providing a reliable method for mental health assessment, our research contributes to the advancement of mental healthcare, facilitating timely and effective support for those in need.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Knowledge Repository for Training Artificial Intelligence Models: Bridging AIML with Decentralized Data
abstract: This paper presents a Blockchain-Based Knowledge Repository (BBKR) tailored for the secure storage and management of training data crucial for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AIML) models. Leveraging Ethereum blockchain technology and smart contracts, the BBKR ensures data integrity, enhances security measures, and promotes decentralization principles. The proposed mechanism includes a detailed explanation of data validation processes, decentralized access control, and scalable transaction mechanisms. Our empirical evaluations validate the efficacy of BBKR in upholding data integrity, enhancing scalability, and fortifying security provisions. The results show significant improvements in data management performance compared to traditional centralized repositories. This research underscores the transformative potential of BBKR in revolutionizing AIML data management paradigms and offers a robust foundation for further advancements in the field. Future work will explore real-world applications and potential enhancements using advanced cryptographic techniques.

articleTitle: Ethnomedicines of Assam and Meghalaya States in India: An Effort to Create Sustainable Livelihoods Among Tribal Communities via App Agroshadhi
abstract: This paper presents a viable solution to bridge the significant gap in the utilization of indigenous medicinal knowl-edge among the tribal communities (TCs), exacerbated by their economic challenges, particularly in the scheduled tribes (STs) of the north-eastern states in India. Apparently, through empirical studies, the traditional knowledge of medicinal plant species has been insufficiently tapped owing to non-commercialization and scaling-up, discarding the proven clinical and pharmacological efficacy. To effectively tackle this multifaceted issue, our solution involves the development of an Android application (App named Agroshadhi) equipped with a diverse range of features, designed to streamline user interaction and enhance accessibility to traditional healthcare solutions. The App has been developed using the Android Studio and Google Firebase for a scalable and reliable realization of data provision, authentication, and content delivery based on its real-time database, cloud storage, authentication, and hosting capabilities. The task of the App entails the TCs to post data on native drugs via a trained middleman App-operator which shall further flow this data towards critical evaluation, validation, marketing, and electronic (e) payments. Consequently, effective management of traditional drug knowledge transfer has been prototyped and presented in this work via an App for more than 300 ethnomedicines obtained via snowball sampling and baseline data capture through field surveys and workshops in Assam and Meghalaya states of India.

articleTitle: Real-Time Estimation of Smart Grids: A Neural Network-Based Unscented Kalman Filter Approach
abstract: Dynamic state estimations in the control centres hold an important role in formulating the current operating scenario of the grid while the states may fluctuate rapidly due to varying load scenarios. Unscented Kalman filters (UKFs) are a class of such aforesaid estimators that are based on the state prediction model, thus depending vastly on the convergence and the accuracy of the estimated states for the previous time step. To effectively develop an accurate state prediction model under varying load scenarios along with improving the estimation accuracy of the UKF, this work undertakes recurrent neural network structures incorporating convolution neural networks (CNNs) and gated recurrent units (GRUs). The CNNs are effectively deployed for feature extraction from time series data of state variables while the GRUs are implemented for an enhanced prediction of the estimated states in real-time. With efficient model training followed by error minimization for the UKF, the estimation accuracy of such dynamic state estimators has been enhanced. The simulation results when carried out over the IEEE 14 bus system promote the efficacy of the developed approach against traditional state estimation techniques under varying load scenarios. The developed model also showcases a real-time power system state estimation under varying noise margins as well.

articleTitle: Implementation of Wavelet Transform Based Convolution Neural Network Method for Detecting Image Forgery
abstract: The traditional forgery methods are not able to detect forgery images due to latest development in software to edit original images. A highly sophisticated technique to be developed to detect image forgery of new images which is edited with high end modern editing tools. At present, image forgery detection is a one of the challenging task to detect whether an image is from authorized or unauthorized. In some criminal cases images are the major evidence to prove criminal by forensic departments. Forensic departments are to use new methods to detect image forgery which will be useful to investigate criminal cases further. In this paper, we proposed discrete wallet transform and CNN method to detect image forgery. First input images are preprocessed then apply CNN method to identify image forgery into either slicing or copy move. The performance of proposed method is compared with existing algorithm and our method shown better results.

articleTitle: An Exploratory Study of 2D Monolayer MoS2 Field Effect Transistors to Exploit Low-power and Energy-efficient Devices: A QuantumATK Tool-Based Approach
abstract: A revolutionary development in nanoelectronics has been the advancement of two-dimensional (2D) materials offers significant opportunities for high-performance devices. Its exceptional electrical properties at the nanoscale make monolayer molybdenum disulphide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) an attractive candidate for field-effect transistors (FETs). A comprehensive characterization of monolayer MoS2 double gate field effect transistor (DGFET) is presented using QuantumATK, a powerful computational tool that enables monolayer MoS2 DGFET to be designed, simulated and characterised in an integrated manner. As a result of this work, electrical properties such as I-V Characteristics, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf>, drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) and subthreshold swing (SS) are investigated. The key properties are highlighted in relation to the International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS) 2023. As a result of this study, various applications within a variety of sectors can be powered by environmentally conscious, power-efficient electronic devices.

articleTitle: A Hybrid ML-Digital Twin Approach for Urban Traffic Optimization
abstract: Urban traffic congestion is a critical challenge facing modern cities worldwide. As urban populations grow, the increasing stress on transportation infrastructure leads to extended journey durations, increased gasoline usage, and heightened environmental contamination, and a diminished quality of life for city dwellers. Traditional traffic management systems have limited ability to handle these issues and often struggle to keep pace with the dynamic and complex nature of urban traffic patterns. To address this problem, this study demonstrates a hybrid system that integrates machine learning (ML) algorithms with digital twin technology. The proposed work is evaluated using four ML models and two statistical parameters: Mean Squared Error (MSE) and coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). This approach main aim is to provide a more efficient and adaptive solution to urban traffic optimization, potentially revolutionizing how cities manage their transportation networks.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Folded Cascode and Recyclic Folded Cascode Operational Amplifier
abstract: This paper presents compensation technique using Single Miller Compensation Nulling Resistor (SMCNR) for improving gain & PSRR of Folded Cascode operational amplifier (FC op-amp) and Recyclic Folded Cascode operational amplifier (RFC op-amp). The conventional FC op-amp provides gain of 55.44dB and PSRR of 36.51dB. When one MOSFET compensation technique is used 129.19 dB (133.03% improvement) gain and 73.71 dB (101.85% improvement) PSRR is obtained for FC op-amp. Moreover, 2 MOSFET compensation technique provides gain of 110.96 dB (100.15% improvement) and PSRR of 55.52 dB (52.03% improvement). Furthermore, conventional RFC op-amp provides gain of 77.18dB and PSRR of 29.54dB. RFC op-amp with 1 MOSFET compensation provides gain of 135.81 dB (75.96% improvement) and PSRR is 60.01 dB (103.17% improvement). Moreover, 2 MOSFET compensation technique provides gain and PSRR of 123.65 dB (60.21% improvement) and 46.46 dB (57.27% improvement) respectively. All simulation results are obtained in cadence virtuoso using SCL 180nm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Sim-MedNet: A Simple Deep Learning Framework for the Classification and Comparative Analysis of Medical Image
abstract: In a wide range of tests and treatments, X-ray imaging examinations are acknowledged as helpful medical tools. Without having to create an incision, it can assist medical professionals in visualizing the body. They can use this to identify, track, and treat a variety of medical disorders. Deep learning technology has recently been employed in a variety of sectors to analyze medical images, and it excels at tasks like segmentation and registration. In this paper, we proposed a new deep learning framework Sim-MedNet to classify seven human bone images e.g., elbow, finger, forearm, hand, humerus, shoulder, and wrist from the MURA dataset, and compared the result of our proposed model with six other neural network models. We also tried to achieve a decent model performance (maximization of accuracy and minimization of loss) utilizing optimizers like Adam, AdaDelta, AdaGrad, Nadam, RMSprop, SGD Momentum, and SGD Nesterov Momentum. The network architecture was trained to achieve the best possible model parameters, improving training efficiency and exceeding performance levels in the classification tasks of musculoskeletal radiographs. Some state-of-the-art models, like GoogleNet and AlexNet, require significant computational resources and time, making them impractical for real-time or resource-constrained applications. This work addressed the issue and achieved 92.27 % accuracy using the entire MURA dataset and 88.74% accuracy with half of it using our proposed framework, surpassing most state-of-the-art methods. Overall, this work presents a practical, reliable, and efficient approach for medical image diagnosis, offering high accuracy in assisting radiologists.

articleTitle: Enhancing PDK Device Library Analysis with XDIRCELL: A Cell-Level Comparison
abstract: This paper presents a Unix shell script designed to automate the comparison of cell libraries between different Process Design Kits (PDKs) in a CADENCE® environment. The script streamlines the process by checking input paths, extracting relevant data, and creating a structured output directory. It includes functionality to decrypt SKILL files and OpenAccess files. The utility leverages a graphical ‘smartdiff’ tool for a clear visual comparison and offers batch mode capabilities, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of PDK management in IC design workflows. The script concludes with an optional cleanup feature, ensuring a tidy workspace post-comparison. This tool optimizes the benefits of automation in the EDA sector by facilitating a more efficient and error resistant PDK cell comparison process with decrypted files. This tool aims to minimize the manual efforts by generating the output in approx. a minute. This script is developed for the use of pdk developers, but it can be further extended to layout and schematic designers for basic xor comparison in the designs.

articleTitle: A Compact Implantable Antenna for Brain Computer Interface Application at ISM Band
abstract: Implantable Brain Computer Interfaces (BCIs) are intended to investigate brain function, send control signals for prosthetic devices in real time, and/or replace lost sensory data due to illness or injury. In this paper, brain implanted antenna designs, analysis, and simulations are presented for Brain Computer Interface (BCI) application. Small implantable antennas frequently exhibit omnidirectional radiation patterns, making them unsuitable for use in in-to-out wireless body area networks. This issue is resolved by the suggested design, which alter the antenna structure inside a realistic brain implant scenario, a seven-layer brain phantom that consists of Dura, Bone, Fat, Skin, Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), Grey, and White matters. The antenna is round measuring 9.88mm in radius and 0.5 mm in thickness. After modeling the seven-layer phantom using full-wave simulation software HFSS, the antenna was inserted in the dura layer (top of the head). The antenna was tuned such that it would radiate widely at a resonating frequency of 2.4 GHz. Taconic RF-35, a biocompatible PCB material with low loss, was used to create the optimal antenna design. Compared to conventional implantable single band antennas which are operating at 2.4 GHz, the suggested antenna has a broader −10-dB impedance bandwidth of 17.24% and simulated peak realized gain of −21dB. In addition, the specific absorption rate (SAR) was computed and evaluated for accordance with IEEE safety criteria.

articleTitle: QoE Comparison between Multi-User OFDMA and Reliable Groupcast for Wireless LAN Audiovisual Transmission
abstract: This paper compares video and audio QoE of OFDMA multi-user transmission and reliable groupcast over wireless LAN. We assume video and audio transmission to several terminals simultaneously. As a reliable groupcast method, we employ Unsolicited Retry, a technique of IEEE 802.11aa GroupCast with Retries. We utilize IEEE 802.11ax for OFDMA transmission. We evaluate application-level QoS by computer simulation. We then assess QoE through a subjective experiment with video and audio streams generated by the output timing obtained from the simulation. We notice that each method has a situation to be applied appropriately.

articleTitle: Power Quality Enhancement Using Cuk Modified Bridgeless Rectifier with Dual Output for Grid Fed Low Power SRM Drive
abstract: This paper is focused on design of a single-phase totem pole bridgeless converter with a dual output (SPTPBLDO) AC-DC converter, derived from Cuk-SEPIC bridgeless configuration, used for high voltage low power (HVLP) grid fed switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive. A rectifier with fewer components in the PFC converter operation leads to reduced conduction losses, making it ideal for use in low-cost, low-power SRM drive. For SRM drive wide-range speed control, DC link voltage of dual output PFC converter is varied by selecting the discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) operation of SPTPBLDO converter. SPTPBLDO converter effectively regulates DC link voltage while also preserving power quality on supply side as the international IEEE/IEC standards. Performance of presented converter for a 450 W SRM drive is validated through MATLAB Simulink. Simulation results have assured compliance of design of low-cost converter-fed SRM drive.

articleTitle: Design of an 8 Bit 1 GSPS Flash ADC with a Latency Induced Thermometric to Binary Encoder
abstract: In this article a 8 bit 1GHz Flash ADC is proposed. Analog front end of the flash ADC consists of Threshold-Inverter-Quantizer (TIQ) based comparators. The digital backend consists of a novel thermometric to binary encoder, capable of performing at required sampling speed without loss of any linearity. Unlike the multiplexer based implementation of thermometric to binary encoder, the present encoder design is based on increasing the latency, without compromising on the throughput. Such latency is inserted in the encoder design by using a 7-step time sampling of digital data. Time sampling is performed using simple D-FFs, which all operate at a sampling speed of 1 GSPS. Using a MUX based 255-to-8 bit thermometric to binary encoder in a flash ADC with TIQ based comparators provide only 5.57 bits of effective number of bits (ENOB) at a sampling speed of 1 GSPS. Whereas the proposed encoder when used in the similar flash ADC topology, improves the ENOB to 7.013 bits. The latency of the ADC output is found to be 3.5 clock cycles.

articleTitle: Optimizing Resume Parsing Processes by Leveraging Large Language Models
abstract: In the present era of internet revolution, organizations have to go through numerous resumes in order to identify the most suitable candidates for their Job Description (JD), while ensuring that no acquisition of talent is overlooked through human mistakes. Thus, tools like Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) have taken over the human process of resume screening, enabling assessment of thousands of resumes in a matter of seconds. Although these technologies are incredibly effective, they are not flawless. Consequently, highly qualified individuals may miss out on said opportunities if their resumes are not formatted correctly. Therefore, individuals must ensure that their resume is appropriately structured prior to submitting it to any organization. The study centers on the present literature and suggests an enhanced approach for parsing resumes by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs).

articleTitle: Impact of Natural Dust on PV Module During Winter in a Suburb of Bangladesh: A Case Study
abstract: The performance of photovoltaic (PV) modules is determined by a variety of factors, including natural dust. This study focuses on the performance of PV modules exposed to dust during the dry season in a Bangladeshi suburb. Data was collected in the study region from December 2022 to February 2023. The results reveal that on a normal sunny day, the clean module accumulates 26.56% more energy than the dusty one. Dust deposition causes a decrease in daily irradiance throughout a sunny week. Cumulative energy shows that the average difference between accumulated energy in January and February for the selected days is 18%. It means during the winter season in the studied area the module accumulates more dust if there is no rain, and the accumulation of the energy could vary up to 18% on average than a clean solar module.

articleTitle: Novel Robust Classifier for Power Quality Disturbances in AC Microgrid
abstract: Modern day power system, is radically different from the conventional power system. The integration of renew-able energy resources, FACTS devices and enhanced power elec-tronics have added to the transients and non-linearity. These are collectively referred as power quality disturbance (PQD). Further, the Inclusion of IoT, communication channels in power system to enable real-time monitoring, have led to the distortion of data. The presented article presents a novel methodology to classify the power quality disturbances in an AC microgrid with high efficacy. The proposed methodology have been implied on simulated noise less and noisy data of voltage signals in microgrid. ML based classifiers are then applied on distinct time domain and frequency based classifiers, and the performance of method is then compared on basis of various metrics. The present work intends to open a new pathway for the PQD classification techniques in the era of communication, often distorting the data signals.

articleTitle: FakeTweet Busters: A Combination of BERT and Deepfake Detection to Resolve the Spreading of Fake AI Generated News
abstract: The spread of misinformation through social media, particularly fake tweets, poses a significant challenge. This work proposes a novel multimodal approach for detecting fake tweets, combining textual and visual analysis. We leverage the strengths of BERT, a pretrained transformer model, for comprehensive textual analysis, and VGG19, a convolutional neural network, for image feature extraction. Additionally, we incorporate deepfake detection to address manipulated visuals. For tweets containing both text and images, a multi-head self-attention mechanism effectively fuses the textual and visual features extracted by BERT and VGG19, respectively. This combined approach aims to achieve superior accuracy in identifying fake tweets compared to methods solely focused on text or image.

articleTitle: Unlocking Potential: A Machine Learning Approach to Job Category Prediction
abstract: India's high unemployment rate (53.4%, ILO Department of Statistics, n.d.) despite a reasonable literacy rate (76.32%, Statista, 2024) suggests a mismatch between skills and job availability. This research addresses this using machine learning to identify suitable job categories for individuals. We explore various techniques like TF-IDF for word embedding, feature selection methods like cross-correlation with Rank-Sum, and different classifiers to predict job categories based on job descriptions and responsibilities. Data from Kaggle is used for training. The primary focus is to find the most effective approach for distinguishing job categories.

articleTitle: Estimation of Glycated Hemoglobin Using Multiwavelength Photoplethysmography Signal
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disorder, and pro-longed exposure to sugar molecules in the blood stream results in hemoglobin glycation. It is measured in percentage of glycated hemoglobin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{HbA}_{1\mathrm{c}})$</tex> cells in all hemoglobin cells. A suspected person may have symptoms such as abrupt weight loss, increased thirst and hunger, frequent urination, etc. The conventional method requires invasive blood testing methods performed in specific laboratories. The work proposes a non-invasive solution to measure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\%\mathbf{HbA}_{1\mathrm{c}}$</tex> using Photoplethysmography (PPG) signal. A PPG sensor records these signals at two distinct wavelengths, i.e., green and infrared (IR). After initial preprocessing and feature extraction, a random forest regressor estimates the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\%\mathbf{HbA}_{1\mathrm{c}}$</tex>. The study is validated with recording of 9 subjects. The estimation of the results shows a high degree of correlation with 0.907 and 0.952 pearson's correlation coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{r}$</tex> values for the reflective PPG signal. These calculated values are compared with the true <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\%\mathbf{HbA}_{1\mathrm{c}}$</tex> values. The results show a close approximation of the calculated values to the true values. Also, the error analysis is performed in terms of mean squared and root mean squared error.

articleTitle: Improved Initialization for Tunicate Swarm Optimization in Cloud Task Scheduling
abstract: Efficient task scheduling in cloud computing is critical for optimizing resource utilization and reducing execution cost. However, the task scheduling problem is known to be NP-hard, motivating the use of metaheuristic algorithms. This paper proposes an improved initialization approach for the Tuni-cate Swarm Optimization (TSO) algorithm, leveraging strategic heuristics. Specifically, Shortest Job First Priority (SJFP) and Earliest Completion Time (ECT) heuristics are employed to initialize TSO. Both of the proposed SJFP-TSO and ECT-TSO algorithms are evaluated on the performance metrices including minimizing makespan, total execution time, load balancing, and energy consumption. Comparative analysis shows the superiority of the proposed algorithms over conventional TSO method.

articleTitle: Economical Demand-Side Management with Distributed Energy Resources
abstract: A potent technology for demand response is proposed in this paper. The proposed algorithm is believed to bring significant monetary increments and improvements in grid stability, especially within the emerging context of renewables as well as Electric Vehicles (EVs). This research presents an innovative strategy for finding residential participants with load profiles alone for maintaining grid stability, which is useful in data-scarce countries like India. The proposed algorithm aimed at maximizing customer and grid benefits. Additionally, the adoption of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) will make Demand Side Management (DSM) strategies more effective, thus underlining their significance in molding a sustainable energy environment. More importantly, the study contributes to the knowledge of economic DSM practices outlining DER integration for future energy resilience and sustainability.

articleTitle: Time Series Forecasting in Financial Market: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Approach for Stock Price Prediction
abstract: Stock market nature is nonlinear, and research on it has become increasingly important in recent years. The influence of numerous factors on stock prices renders stock forecasting an intricate and demanding task. Possible stock market price forecast increases people's gains while minimizing their risks. Ma-chine learning and deep learning techniques play an important role in forecasting stock prices in today's scenario, considering technical indicators. The choice of deep learning technique and tweaking its hyper-parameters are crucial components of stock price prediction. Several model architectures are suggested here, taking into account LSTM deep learning techniques and hyper-parameters like the batch size, number of hidden layers and number of epochs.
