Hyper-parameters such as the number of years data, the number of preceding days considered, and database spitting are examined and discussed here, in addition to hyper-parameters relating to LSTM networks. The model with 11 years of historical data, 60 or 100 previous days consideration, and 70:10:20 database split outperforms as compared to other model architectures suggested in the paper.

articleTitle: Implementation of IoMT-Assisted Smart Healthcare Monitoring for Clinical Infectious Diseases
abstract: Contactless interactions are more common in recent years due to advances in technology and consumer demand for the convenience of touch-free transactions. In this work, a nursing assist for hospitals is proposed which can reduce the risk of infection by decreasing the interactions with the patients. Nurses have to take rounds at least twice a day for the health check-up and doctors spend a part of their consultation time for the daily check-up of each in-patient. Therefore, the proposed device assists the nurses by monitoring the patient's health such as measuring temperature, heart rate and oxygen saturation level periodically using sensors. The medical report of the patient can be stored in the cloud and accessed from the nursing station. From the database, the doctors can analyze the patient's health easily and can change the way of treatment if needed. The proposed device here can avoid the systematic and tedious rounds by nurses and doctors and also improves the patient satisfaction. This machine could be a key system to help and drive down the costs of care and human labour.

articleTitle: Improving Electric Network Frequency Estimation Through Combined ENF Enhancement and ROOT MUSIC Algorithm
abstract: Electric Network Frequency (ENF) estimation is a critical component in various applications, including forensic audio analysis and synchronization of multimedia recordings. Previous research has primarily focused on enhancing identification accuracy from noisy ENF signals, with noise posing a challenge to accurate frequency peak detection. Rather than solely addressing noise reduction, this paper proposes an approach by integrating ENF enhancement techniques with the ROOT-MUSIC algorithm. The established ENF enhancement methods are combined with the high-resolution ROOT-MUSIC algorithm to enhance frequency estimation accuracy. This study showcases the effectiveness of this integration, demonstrating improved accuracy in ENF frequency estimation compared to existing methods. Experimental results on real-world data substantiate the benefits of this combined approach. The proposed technique not only contributes to accurate ENF estimation but also has potential applications in various domains where precise frequency analysis is crucial.

articleTitle: Study of Transfer Learning Technique for Handwritten Devanagari Character Recognition
abstract: In recent years, many researchers have investigated the techniques for recognition of handwritten letters from images. It is an important application for historical document analysis and other applications like content reading from images. The recognition of characters from handwritten images is a challenging task due to huge variation in handwriting from person to person. The transfer learning technique have been used for performing such classification with higher accuracy. This paper proposes Devanagari script recognition using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. The transfer learning technique is used to tune the pretrained models for classification. Three CNN architectures, VGG16, VGG19 and ResNet have been used for classification and their performances have been compared. The proposed model using VGG16,VGG19 and ResNet is observed to demonstrate higher accuracy of 99.07%, 99.17%, and 99.17% as compared to the existing works.

articleTitle: Impact Assessment of Heat Waves on Resilience of Power System Components
abstract: Heat waves is a significant climatic phenomenon exerting profound effects on society, agriculture, the environment, and crucially, the power sector. This study aims to assess the impact of heat waves on power system components, particularly transmission lines and generators. A normal distribution model is employed to synthesize the historical heat wave data for a period of 10 years and applied to the IEEE 57-bus transmission test system. The resilience of the system components is determined in terms of impact of heat wave on the capacity of transmission lines and power generation output which are temperature-dependent. The resilience is also investigated for base case loading and overloading conditions during heat waves. The other key parameters such as Available Transfer Capability (ATC), system losses, remaining generator capacity, and generation cost are also evaluated to provide an insight into the power system's component resilience under heat wave conditions.

articleTitle: Enhanced Dual-Slope-Based Digitizer for 4-Wire Connected Resistive Sensors
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dual-slope-based digitizer circuit tailored for 4-wire connected resistive sensors. Utilizing cost-effective components, this circuit offers a simple yet robust method for accurate sensor readings. Experimental tests demonstrate the circuit's capability to measure sensor resistance within the range of 60 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex> to 390 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex>, corresponding to a temperature span of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$850^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> using an RTD-Pt100 sensor. The circuit exhibits a maximum nonlinearity error of 0.06 % and a maximum measurement error of 0.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex>, showcasing its high precision. One key advantage of this digitizer is its single measurement cycle requirement, streamlining the measurement process. Additionally, the circuit incorporates constant current excitation to mitigate self-heating effects and minimize its reliance on digital ports, enhancing its speed and reliability in sensor measurements. Moreover, its single-supply operation ensures efficiency, with an average power consumption of approximately 20 mW. These findings underscore the circuit's potential as a cost-effective and efficient solution for a variety of sensing applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Shading on Paddy Field: A Case Study in Bangladesh Towards Agrivoltaic
abstract: Agrivoltaics is the dual use of land by combining agricultural crop production with a photovoltaic (PV) system. In this work, the impact of shading has been analyzed on a particular crop to understand the future prospects of the agrivoltaic system on that land. A set up is made on land situated in the Bogura district of Bangladesh. A total of 15 sample crops have been considered from both the shaded and unshaded regions to investigate the grain number, height of the crops, perimeter, and number of small branches. It is evident from the study that, unshaded sample crops have a higher number of grains, have a greater height, and have a larger perimeter than shaded region crops. Though there are some dissimilarities, such as the shaded region sample crop showing a higher grain number, the total grain number shows that unshaded region crops have a higher number of grains. All the data did not exceed the average 30% difference between shaded and unshaded data, which ensures the future implementation prospects of agrivoltaic in that field.

articleTitle: Preserving Seasonal and Trend Information: A Variational Autoencoder-Latent Space Arithmetic Based Approach for Non-Stationary Learning
abstract: AI models have garnered significant research attention towards predictive task automation. However, a stationary training environment is an underlying assumption for most models and such models simply do not work on non-stationary data since a stationary relationship is learned. The existing solutions propose making data stationary prior to model training and evaluation. This leads to loss of trend and seasonal patterns which are vital components for learning temporal dependencies of the system under study. This research aims to address this limitation by proposing a method for enforcing stationary behavior within the latent space while preserving trend and seasonal information. The method deploys techniques including Differencing, Time-series decomposition, and Latent Space Arithmetic (LSA), to learn information vital for efficient approximation of trend and seasonal information which is then stored as embeddings within the latent space of a Variational Autoencoder (VAE). The approach's ability to preserve trend and seasonal information was evaluated on two time-series non-stationary datasets. For predictive performance evaluation, four deep learning models were trained on the latent vector representations of the datasets after application of the proposed method and all models produced competitive results in comparison with state-of-the-art techniques using RMSE as the performance metric.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method to Reduce Power in Built in Self Test
abstract: VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration) industry is at the forefront of technological innovation, continuously pushing the boundaries of chip design and fabrication to create increasingly powerful and efficient electronic devices. Its advancements drive the development of everything from smartphones and computers to IoT devices and automotive electronics, shaping the way we live and interact with technology. Circuit testing is crucial within the VLSI industry, wherein the output of a design is assessed against its performance. BIST (Built-In Self-Test) is a method that involves incorporating a Test Pattern Generator (TPG), Output Response Analyzer (ORA) and the main Design under Test (DUT) directly on to the chip. One of the challenges faced in in-circuit testing is the rise in power consumption. This work aims to generate deterministic patterns, such that it consumes less power while testing DUT. The TPG is developed for ISCAS'89 and EPFL benchmark circuits using Verilog. The proposed technique is synthesized using Synopsys Design Compiler. The percentage improvement in power when compared with Linear feedback shift register (LFSR), Read Only Memory (ROM) plus combinational circuit and binary counter based TPG is in the range of 7-99%, respectively.

articleTitle: Control of WRIG Based WECS for Grid Integration
abstract: This paper presents a transformer-less back to back connected voltage source converter(VSC) configuration of wound rotor induction generator(WRIG) for wind energy conversion system(WECS). The delivery of power to grid from rotor side at same voltage as that of grid is ensured usually by the transformer. A bidirectional DC-DC converter(BDC) is used to replace transformer by providing sufficient magnitude of DC link voltage to the grid side converter(GSC) for grid synchronisation. Simulation results supplement implementation of BDC in between rotor side converter(RSC) an GSC.

articleTitle: Efficient Solar-Battery Powered High Voltage PMSM Drive with Sensorless Vector Control for EV
abstract: This paper presents a novel high voltage permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) topology powered by a low voltage battery and solar photovoltaic (PV) array for electric vehicle (EV) applications. Presented system integrates an intermediate bidirectional DC-DC converter between battery and DC link, which regulates DC link voltage and facilitates battery charging during regenerative braking. A coupled inductor-based DC-DC boost converter is employed as maximum power point tracking (MPPT) converter, ensuring continuous input and output currents while maximizing power extraction from rooftop solar PV. To enhance control of PMSM, a novel sensorless vector control strategy based on a sliding mode observer (SMO) and an improved phase locked loop (PLL) is implemented. This approach mitigates chattering and harmonics, providing accurate speed and position estimation for effective motor control. Designed topology not only improves driving range and efficiency of EV but also reduces reliance on a large battery, thereby lowering overall system costs. Obtained results validate efficacy of proposed system in optimizing power management and enhancing performance of solar-powered EVs.

articleTitle: YAR-Net: Yoga Asanas Recognition Network Based on Variational Autoencoder
abstract: Yoga is a holistic practice aimed at rejuvenating individuals physically, mentally, and spiritually. Despite rapid technological advancements, there remains ample room for computational exploration across various social domains. Yoga image analysis is a nascent field that aims at finding the exact location of yoga postures so that they can recognize the yoga asana more reliably. Yet, yoga asanas recognition is a challenging task that is worsened due to increased dimensionality, and the problem of segmentation, leading to difficulties in recognizing asanas with high precision. To address these challenges, a variational autoencoder-based Yoga asanas recognition network (YAR - Net) is proposed, capable of reliably identifying numerous yoga asanas. The proposed methodology incorporates segmentation from Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (mR-CNN) to identify the Region of Interest (ROI) followed by feature extraction from segmented ROI utilizing Local Binary Patterns (LBP), Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), and Edge features. Finally, recognition of yoga asanas is accomplished by YAR - Net which provides the recognition accuracy of 97.46%, and 99.91% using benchmark datasets Yoga107 and YogaPoses, respectively. The results underscore the YAR - Net's remarkable performance as compared to the state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Surface Defect Detection of Outdoor Insulators in Low-Light Environments
abstract: Outdoor insulators are crucial for maintaining reliable power transmission and distribution. However, inspecting these vital components under low-light conditions is essential to ensure uninterrupted power supply in all weather circumstances. This study employed an image enhancement technique optimized for low-light images and a single-stage object detection model to identify diverse surface defects on insulators. The training dataset comprised 1008 insulator images depicting various surface conditions, including healthy, broken, polluted, and flashed surfaces. As an initial step, a low-light image enhancement method was applied for image pre-processing. Subsequently, the YOLOv9 model was utilized to detect different surface defects. Finally, to facilitate remote application, a web-based app was developed using Gradio, further improving the accessibility and usability of the implemented solution. The results revealed that the YOLOv9c model achieved an impressive mAP@50 of 99.5%. This outstanding performance enables proactive maintenance, minimizes downtime, and enhances power systems' overall security and reliability.

articleTitle: A Novel Quadratic Boost Converter Based on Switched Capacitor for High Voltage Gain Applications
abstract: The paper presents a novel high-gain quadratic boost converter with the benefit of non-pulsating input current, and the inductor's current is relatively low, which results in higher efficiency. The principle of operation is shown in continuous conduction mode (CCM). The proposed converters offer high step-up voltage by combining the Switched Capacitor(SC) based quadratic boost converter. Compared to conventional quadratic boost converters, the proposed converter has low inductor current and very little voltage stress across the active power switches of the output voltage, resulting in better efficiency and a low-cost semiconducting device with less cost. The proposed converter is designed, and its simulations are proofread and verified in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Innovative Approach: CNNs for Heart Disease Prediction
abstract: The fact that heart disease is still a health concern emphasizes the necessity of precise and effective techniques for early identification and diagnosis. The aim of this work is to investigate the general behavior of most machine learning algorithms. Analyzing a dataset comprising a spectrum of demographic data from people both with and without cardiac disease forms part of the study. Our suggested approach intends to assess and compare, for heart disease risk, the predictive capability of machine learning techniques. Among the methods under study are decision trees, random forests, support vector machines, logistic regression, k closest neighbors, and suggested CNN. The results suggest that various machine learning algorithms show levels of capabilities. Random Forests display accuracy and reliability while CNNs demonstrate their potential in capturing connections within the data and occasionally achieving higher accuracy than Random Forests. Support Vector Machines and Logistic Regression also exhibit performance. This study adds to the expanding research on predicting heart disease by providing an analysis of machine learning techniques.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Techniques and Its impact on Human Consciousness and Healthcare
abstract: The IT industry has benefited greatly from the development of artificial intelligence (AI) in the healthcare sector. Analyzing the connections between healthcare practices and patient outcomes is the goal of AI approaches connected to health. AI will be useful in the healthcare industry going forward because to the complexity and growth of data in this sector. Its capability aids in the production of accurate health reports, statistics, appropriate diagnostic techniques, etc. for both physicians and patients. AI has emerged as the greatest rescuer, providing connections between genetic codes or even surgical support. This falls under several primary categories, including medication development, personalized medicine, administrative tasks, patient monitoring, patient involvement and adherence, and diagnosis and treatment recommendations. The paper reviews a number of AI concepts, including computers with human intelligence, applications in neurology, and disease diagnostics. For artificial intelligence to be used in healthcare more practically, the primary challenges still need to be addressed. It is crucial to develop AI algorithms that can be explained as well as to collect extensive data.

articleTitle: Bio Inspired Methods for Intrusion Detection in Internet of Things: A Survey
abstract: IoT has evolved in last few years and have become part of our lives, and thus lot of data is generated through these IoT systems. This advancement has motivated attackers to process intrusion in the system and manipulate data and process for the same. Network has a major role in IoT systems and Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) is designed to protect it by identifying different kinds of attacks and unauthorized applications or users. To secure these IoT systems, various tools and techniques have been evolved, that ranges from basic securing algorithms to bio inspired algorithms, Usage of Bio Inspired algorithms has features selection process as an essential to create a successful network IDS. Different bio-inspired algorithms are employed to categorize features more precisely, quickly determine whether network traffic is odd or regular, and recognize various attack types. This paper attempts a survey on usage of some of the bio-inspired algorithms those can be used for Intrusion Detection in IoT environment and identifies how artificial Immune system can be better than other techniques for the feature selection or classification process.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Solar PV Fed Sensorless BLDC Motor Control Using of PR Controller and EMF Observer
abstract: This paper presents Solar PV Fed Sensorless BLDC motor drive with Proportional Resonant (PR) Controller based speed control. Detailed modelling of PR controller-based system is also included in the paper. A Back-EMF observer-based hysteresis band controller for sensorless commutation of the motor is implemented. The system consists of solar PV panel, boost converter, BLDC motor, and PR controller and is simulated in MATLAB Simulink. The system is tested under steady state and dynamic conditions. The results presented in the paper verify the stable operation of the system under all the operation conditions. A detailed performance comparison of presented system with conventional PI controller-based system is also included in the paper. The comparison shows improved speed regulation and better dynamic performance of the system.

articleTitle: A Novel Ensemble Deep Learning Approach for Robust Multi-class Hair Fall Disease Classification
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of hair fall diseases is crucial but often relies on limited dermatologist access. A deep-learning ensemble approach for automating hair fall disease classification from dermatological images. Traditional methods involving visual inspection are subjective and error-prone. Our approach leverages state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs), including VGG-16, VGG-19, and MobileNet-V2, with an ensemble model averaging strategy to combine predictions and improve performance. Extensive experiments on a curated dataset demonstrate remarkable results, with the ensemble model achieving 99 % accuracy on the test set. This automated system has the potential to reduce subjectivity, improve accessibility, aid early diagnosis, and reduce burdens on healthcare systems. A comprehensive analysis is provided, including the dataset, architectures, training process, evaluation metrics, and insights into challenges and future research directions. The source code and models are publicly released: GitHub Repository.

articleTitle: Impact of V2G/G2V on Voltage Stability in Distribution Networks
abstract: This paper presents a technology such as Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) that can potentially play a significant role in voltage regulation. The system can schedule day-ahead Electric Vehicle (EV) charging and discharging to reduce EV ownership and charging costs through participating in voltage regulation services. A power system with V2G/G2V integration is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment to evaluate the performance of the different control strategies. The results demonstrate that centralized control delivers the best performance in terms of frequency regulation precision, but it is also the most difficult and expensive to install. Decentralized management is quicker and cheaper to establish, but it provides a lower level of frequency management.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Real-Time Remote Patient Monitoring System with Incorporation of Physical Activity in Closed Loop Diabetes Management
abstract: Diabetes, a chronic medical condition characterised by elevated levels of glucose in the blood, creates difficulties in regulating glucose balance, leading to potential severe health implications. The management of diabetes has been revolutionised by continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices; however, their usefulness is limited because they are not usually integrated with data on physical activity. To address this gap, this study describes a cloud-based remote patient monitoring system that seamlessly connects continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices with physical activity tracking to improve diabetes management. Using machine learning techniques on cloud platforms such as Google Cloud Platform (GCP), the system makes real-time adjustments to insulin dosage based on estimates of blood glucose levels. The cloud-based architecture makes data processing and storage scalable, safe, and efficient, making it possible to manage massive volumes of continuous monitoring data effectively. CPU utilisation peaked at just 10% during server testing with a load of 10 users per compute engine instance, suggesting strong performance and scalability. Post-testing, CPU utilisation remained low at 0.63 %. Typical usage situations produced 1.03 KiBts outgoing and 0.53 KiBts inbound data rates and write data rate was 6.39 KBts despite constant read rates. The use of physical activity data improves the prediction accuracy of glucose levels, enabling customised and prompt responses. Through an intuitive mobile application interface, the system provides patients and healthcare providers with real-time data retrieval and remote access. Preliminary testing demonstrates robust performance and positive feedback, paving the way for further refinements, integration optimizations, and clinical trials to evaluate real- world effectiveness.

articleTitle: Autoencoder Aided Semi-supervised Incremental Learning of Handwritten Characters
abstract: Incremental learning is an important feature of next generation machine learning systems - it is about learning new classes incrementally by training on labeled images of the new classes. When the availability of the labeled images is limited, unlabeled images that are easily available, can be utilized in image classification using semi-supervised learning techniques. We demonstrate for the first time, the semi-supervised learning together with the incremental learning in neural network aided by auto-encoder. At first, an under-complete convolutional auto-encoder is trained on the unlabeled images of all the anticipated classes. Then, the pretrained encoder acting as feature extractor, is integrated with the classifier layers constructing a custom VGG network. Subsequently, the VGG model is trained on the labeled images incrementally in task incremental fashion keeping the feature extractor parameters unchanged. In our experiments on the EMNIST (extended MNIST) dataset, we obtain incremental learning accuracy of more than 96 % when the model is trained on 2000 labeled images for each class in the incremental learning phase. Due to the pretraining with the unlabeled images, our model performs well, even with fewer labeled images for training in the incremental learning phase; we obtain accuracy of more than 92 % even when the number of labeled images is reduced to 500 images for each class. We also present experimental results for the case, where the autoencoder is pretrained on randomly cropped images instead of the full images, thus learning from the partial features of the images. Despite using images that are cropped, we obtain incremental learning accuracy comparable to the result obtained for full images. The method proposed here may be useful in next generation machine learning applications due to the dual benefits of incremental learning and semi-supervised learning.

articleTitle: An Optimal Review of Deep Learning Algorithms for Object Detection
abstract: Computer vision, a vital facet of deep learning, seamlessly integrates object localization and classification techniques to attain precise outcomes. Deep learning, nestled within the broader realm of machine learning, leverages neural networks as its fundamental algorithm. Particularly in the domain of images and computer vision, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) reign supreme. Over the years, numerous researchers have innovated state-of-the-art models by tailoring the foundational CNN architecture in diverse manners. This paper undertakes a comparative analysis of several models, evaluating their performance based on metrics such as mean average precision (MAP) or accuracy across various datasets. Additionally, we intend to quantify their computational complexity, measured in floating-point operations (FLOPs), employing a TensorFlow profiler.

articleTitle: Geospatial Data Analysis for Restaurant Business Strategies and Urban Planning
abstract: Geospatial data analysis is a crucial tool in various domains, including urban planning and environmental studies to business strategies and healthcare. This research paper presents a comprehensive approach to geospatial data analysis using clustering techniques and heatmaps. Clustering techniques offer the ability to identify patterns and group similar data points, while heatmaps visually represent the density or intensity of specific attributes across different locations on a map. The paper discusses the challenges of applying clustering techniques to geospatial analysis and presents a methodology that leverages geocoding techniques and kernel density estimation for heatmaps generation. The results and discussions section showcases the insights derived from the generated heatmaps, such as identifying popular dining areas, assessing restaurant quality, and understanding customer preferences. The implications of this research extend to restaurant business strategies, urban planning, and decision-making processes. The findings can guide location selection, menu offerings, and marketing strategies for businesses, as well as inform urban planners in identifying areas of high dining activity for infrastructure planning.

articleTitle: Malware Trend in Smart Grid Cyber Security
abstract: Cybersecurity is one of the building blocks of a current complex smart grid that has multi-faceted dimensions. Since the Ukraine grid attack in 2015, worldwide, electricity utilities have had to bolster the cyber defence posture in the growing realm of cyber-attacks. One of the noteworthy cyber-attack types is malware, which extensively uses SCADA in the operational technology domain of the power sector. The massive amount of data collected and managed in the cyber world invariably raises the danger of network system vulnerability. Given the likelihood of the dark web's members being similarly intelligent, the growing complexity of IT-OT (information technology and operations technology) interwoven systems raises concerns about cyber threats to the electrical utility. Some of the OT malware transpired chronologically when analysed, providing scope for observing the malicious trend and the corresponding potential in the future.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis Of Voltage Doubler And Diode Rectifier For LCC Converter In DC-DC Charging Systems
abstract: In this research two popular solutions for full-budge resonant LCC (Inductor-Capacitor-Capacitor) converter for DC-DC charging systems are compared, i.e. diode rectifier and voltage doubler. Through simulations with a 20-40V input, the paper analyzes voltage gain, efficiency, and ripple factor. The proposed voltage doubler achieves a maximum efficiency of 62.13% and a ripple factor of 0.68, surpassing the performance of the diode rectifier. Additionally, the paper presents a comprehensive study of the converter's output voltage, current, input, efficiency, and ripple factor under varying input voltage conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Insurance Claim Fraud Detection Through Advanced Data Analytics Techniques
abstract: Insurance claim fraud is a significant problem that can cost insurers millions of dollars each year. The use of advanced data analytics techniques such as machine learning, data mining, and natural language processing can help insurance companies to detect and prevent fraudulent activities. In this research paper, this proposes a methodology for insurance claim fraud detection that involves data collection, preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, training, evaluation, tuning, and deployment. Also discuss the experimental setup for insurance claim and fraud detection and future scope for research in this area. Our findings suggest that the use of advanced analytics techniques can significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of fraud detection systems, enabling insurers to detect and prevent fraudulent activities in a timely and efficient manner.

articleTitle: Real-Time AQI Forecasting With High-Throughput Using IoT Devices
abstract: This work explores the real-time and high-throughput decision-making of the Air Quality Index (AQI) and the pollutants concerning commercially available IoT-based de-vices such as GPU and Raspberry Pi. The proposed methodology trains various parameterized algorithms to investigate the best suitable settings that could effectively forecast the future values of AQI, and concerning pollutants. The algorithm with the best performance has been further deployed on different commercially available computing devices for analyzing the throughput. The employed experimental set-up successfully evaluates the best suitable algorithm i.e. Random Forest (RF), with a coefficient of determination (Adj. R2) 0.82. Additionally, deploying the RF algorithm on coral TPU-embedded Raspberry Pi 4 provides 3–11 fold relative enhancement in throughput comparison to CPU, GPU, and Raspberry Pi 4.

articleTitle: The Implementation and Research of Fault Prevention Emergency Automatic for Power Systems
abstract: The Mongolian central energy system operates in parallel with the Russian energy system through 220kV overhead lines 257th and 258th. Up to 345MW of electricity is imported through the overhead transmission line during the winter peak. In this regard, the center's energy system was modeled and tested on the Powerfactory program in connection with the system's stability by automatically reducing the frequency of the system, preventing the system's frequency from falling to zero during peak loads.

articleTitle: A Review: Smart Wristwear for Alzheimer Patients with an Advanced Tracking System
abstract: Globally, there are around 50 million individuals afflicted with dementia, including Alzheimer's disease. When caregivers are unable to be with the afflicted person constantly, conditions like dementia and Alzheimer's can provide a variety of therapeutic obstacles. And it is crucial to ensure the patient's safety and receive the right care, but receiving treatment without the ability to regularly check on the patient's status poses a variety of concerns. Thankfully, there are a number of wearable Internet of Things devices available that can contribute to the highest level of safety and care. IoT has fueled medical research to lower costs and increase accessibility for all. Our solution, which takes into account the significance of these characteristics in the field of healthcare, presents an affordable, efficient, portable, and user-friendly smart wearable device that can be used in conjunction with a mobile application to track, monitor, alert, and support Alzheimer's patients. One of the most promising ways to assist patients and their care takers is through the outcomes of this Internet of Things (IoT)-based healthcare system. The application of AI has grown dramatically in all fields these days. Thus, the combination of AI and IoT technologies can lead to a variety of benefits. Instantaneous evaluation of information using AI can improve the choice-making of the Internet of Things devices. AI can help IoT devices learn and adapt to their environments, improving their ability to provide accurate and timely information. The purpose of this study is to provide information about the different wearable devices present for people with AD.

articleTitle: Rover Attitude Determination Using Kinematics Model and its Applications in Pragyan Operations
abstract: Rover plays an important role in planetary exploration missions. They serve as mobile laboratory traversing over challenging terrains to carry out in situ scientific experiments. One crucial part of path planning is to ensure safety of rover as it traverses uneven terrain covered with boulders & craters. This paper deals with kinematic modelling of a 6-wheel rocker-bogie rover and its application in different phases like design & mission operations. A geometric model of the rover inverse kinematics is developed to compute rover attitude as a function of terrain. This model is used to select a path which has less chances of the rover toppling. The model accuracy is proved by carrying out experiments on calibrated test bed. The application of this model during Pragyan mobility operations, post Chandrayaan-3 landing on 23 Aug, 2024 is illustrated.

articleTitle: Optimization of Power Quality for Single-Phase Grid-Connected Solar PV Using MANF
abstract: This paper introduces a control algorithm based on a modified adaptive notch filter (MANF) aimed at enhancing the power quality for the single-phase grid interfaced solar photovoltaic (PV) system. This paper proposes the modification of the default adaptive notch filter to give the more optimized result for the grid current control. The main goal is to address the mitigation of harmonics from the grid current control. The MANF control is specifically designed to extract the unit template of the grid voltage, and provides significant resistance to power disturbances and thereby ensuring system robustness. To optimize power output from the PV system, a very efficient P&O algorithm based MPPT setup is utilized. A feed-forward term is incorporated to account for the contributions from solar sources, enhancing the system's dynamic response to the changes in solar irradiation. The system's overall performance meets the intended objectives and complies with the IEEE-519 standard, which governs harmonic distortion limits in power systems.

articleTitle: Experience of Flexible Operations in Power System as a System Operator in Western Region of India

abstract: This paper highlights the experience of Flexible operations in power system as a system operator in Western Region of India. System operator plays a pivotal role in maintaining Load-generation balance so as to ensure a secure, reliable and economic grid operation. Electricity Demand is variable in nature and exact delivery of electricity is just a coincidence. Similarly, with the integration of vast Renewable Energy capacity, generation variability is also increasing. In this paper, the overview of seasonal variation of various sources of generation is presented along with the changing pattern of state wise demand in Western Region of India.

articleTitle: Leveraging Grey Wolf Optimization for Multi-Criteria Recommender Systems
abstract: Traditional recommender system makes recommendations to users based on their preferences by utilising overall ratings. However, these recommendations do not accurately reflect the taste of the user. Therefore, inclusion of various criteria ratings into recommender system may be helpful to generate effective recommendations which may reflect accurately user preferences. However,forfeiting the optimal weights of various users on different criteria is a major concern in multi-criteria recommender system. In our proposed work we have employed the capability of grey wolf optimization to find out optimal weights of various users on different criteria and conducted exhaustive empirical study on the ITM-Rec dataset to support our proposed work. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our work in terms of various performance measures.

articleTitle: Low Refractive Index Photonic Crystal Fiber-Based Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of highly sensitive plasmonic micro biosensors, focusing on gold-coated and silver-coated designs using dual-gist photonic crystal fibers (PCF). The study involves graphical and numerical analysis via COMSOL Multiphysics 6.1 simulation. To improve performance, the silver sensor is treated with a thin graphene layer to prevent oxidation, while gold is chosen for its chemical inertness and recyclability. The gold-coated sensor demonstrates maximum sensitivity of 1,15,999 nm/RIU and amplitude of 2450 RIU-l, with resolution values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.66 \ \mathrm{x} \ 10-7$</tex> RIU. The silver-coated sensor shows 49,000 nm/RIU and 1876 RIU-l sensitivity, with a resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.86 \ \mathrm{x} \ 10-6$</tex> and an FOM of 555. The sensors exhibit impressive metrics for refractive index sensing (1.29-1.39 RIU range), making them highly suitable for organic chemical sensing, biological detection, pharmacological assessments, and other analytical applications. Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) allows for studying molecular interactions, such as ligand-receptor binding and RNA-DNA interactions, by measuring changes in SPR angles. Despite advantages, conventional SPR sensors face limitations with traditional designs like Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG), prism-based, and fiber optic methods.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of MA0.9Cs0.1Pb(I0.6Br0.4)3 Based Perovskite Solar Cells Through Numerical Simulations
abstract: In this work, a thorough investigation of methyl ammonium and cesium - based mixed halide perovskite solar cells is performed. Numerical simulations are done on SCAPS-1D simulator to examine the effect of material properties of charge transport layers and perovskite. Further, an optimum interfacial defect concentration of charge transport layers and absorber is examined to quantify the effect of interfacial recombination. Also, the series and shunt resistances are varied for a certain range and performance parameters are determined. The optimum device results in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{O C}=1.464 \mathrm{V}, \text{JSC}=22.60 \text{mA} / \text{cm}^2, \text{FF}=86.57$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta{=}$</tex> 28.67%.

articleTitle: An Efficient Multi-Objective Task Scheduling in Fog-Cloud Environment
abstract: The high communication bandwidth between end-devices and cloud servers along with the associated network latency, renders it infeasible for the modern day Internet of Things (IoT) applications to meet their stringent latency requirements. Hence, it is crucial to process application data closer to the network edge, both optimally and efficiently. To address this concern, we first design a multilayer fog-based loT system architecture. Next, we propose an optimal task scheduling scheme to uniformly distribute tasks amongst the fog nodes on the basis of Quality of Service (QoS) requirements of the application. Our proposed scheduling scheme optimizes delay, energy consumption and fog node utilization simultaneously while considering dependencies amongst sub-tasks in a way, such that delay and energy consumption is minimized whereas fog node utilization is maximized. We evaluate the performance of our proposed scheme both theoretically and experimentally through simulation using the iFogSim simulator. Our results establish that the proposed scheduling scheme efficiently distributes tasks amongst the available fog nodes as well as reduces the energy consumption of the fog nodes by ~ 1.26% compared to a state-of-the-art competitor at the cost of a little extra latency.

articleTitle: Mitigating Overfitting in Deep Learning: Insights from Bayesian Regularization
abstract: Overfitting is one of the most commonly faced challenges when designing a model, it's when model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data. This review explores Bayesian perspectives on regularization techniques for machine learning models. Bayesian regularization incorporates prior knowledge into the fitting process, allowing for a more controlled and probabilistic understanding of the model parameters. An exploration into the theoretical foundations of Bayesian regularization is done by examining parametric and non-parametric Bayesian methods, analyze their potential to improve model generalization and reduce overfitting. Theoretical demonstration and well-known results on simple models and feed forward neural network are presented to emphasize the impact regularization can have on general accuracy and model's generalization capabilities. By synthesizing recent advancements, a set of insights regarding the integration of Bayesian frameworks with traditional regularization strategies is provided. This paper aims to guide future research in developing robust, Bayesian-informed regularization strategies.

articleTitle: Optimizing Personal Finance Management through AI-Driven Decision Support Systems
abstract: The paper explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into decision support systems for personal finance management. As financial landscapes become increasingly complex, traditional approaches often fail to keep pace with evolving market conditions and diverse individual goals. AI-driven systems offer a promising solution by leveraging advanced algorithms to analyze data, predict market trends, and provide personalized recommendations. These systems aim to enhance budgeting, investment strategies, debt management, and retirement planning, thereby empowering individuals to make more informed financial decisions and improve their overall financial health. However, challenges such as data privacy and transparency must be addressed to ensure the responsible deployment of these technologies. This research underscores AI's transformative potential in financial technology, highlighting its role in revolutionizing personal finance management practices.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Early Detection of Heart Attacks from Health Parameters
abstract: Heart disease compromises public health and hospitals all throughout the globe. In this context, early identification of heart attacks is very crucial. Traditional diagnostic techniques are hampered by their reliance on intrusive procedures or a small range of clinical criteria. In this context, this study presents a deep learning-based model for early identification of heart attacks. Using a well-structured neural network model, our method achieves 85 % accuracy in differentiating between heart attack and normality. Although there are still difficulties like class imbalance and model fine-tuning, this study shows the potential of deep learning in enhancing early illness identification.

articleTitle: Enhancing Control of Microsoft Teams Meetings and PowerPoint Presentations Through Gesture Recognition
abstract: Improving human-computer interaction is essential for smooth distant collaboration in the age of digital connectivity. In order to expedite user engagements and enhance the overall experience during virtual meetings and presentations, this project explores the integration of gesture recognition technology with Microsoft Teams and PowerPoint. The system uses a custom-built neural network for gesture classification and MediaPipe for hand pose estimation to identify five predefined hand signs: mute, unmute, camera on, camera off, and no action. Using 500 labeled data points (of which 125 were used for testing), the initial testing produced a 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> accuracy score for all motions. These results were further supported by the categorization report, which showed that the F1-score, precision, and recall all achieved 1.00. These outcomes substantiate the resilience of the used neural network architecture, preprocessing methodologies, and data collection strategies. Although the controlled testing environment yielded encouraging results, the study recognizes that additional tuning is required to guarantee resilience in practical applications. Subsequent research endeavors will center around augmenting the dataset, integrating varied settings, and investigating sophisticated methodologies such as data augmentation and transfer learning. To improve the model's accuracy and adaptability over time, adaptive learning techniques and real-time performance monitoring will also be incorporated. This study shows how gesture recognition can be used to build a virtual collaboration environment that is more user-friendly and productive.

articleTitle: An End-to-End Decentralized Organ Donation and Transplantation System Using Blockchain
abstract: Organ donation allows the patient to have a life enhancing opportunity with a higher quality of life. This article addresses the existing limitations and challenges of current centralized organ donation system by introducing the concept of a decentralized system for organ donation and transplantation using Blockchain Technology. We propose an end-to-end organ donation and transplantation system developed using Hardhat, ReactJS and Metamask. The proposed system ensures a secure and transparent storage of donor and recipient data which can only be altered by authorized entities. Further, the end-to-end system was hosted on Interplanetary File System (IPFS) to enable persistent availability of organ data. We also assess function calls present in various smart contracts of the developed system in terms of computation cost. Deployment of smart contract, and development of decentralised application with both front-end and back-end are the most appealing features of the proposed mechanism which supersedes the existing state-of-the-arts.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition Using GRU and LSTM
abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is a hot topic in research, with applications in human-computer interaction, mental health screening, and customer service. In this research, our objective is to develop an accurate and reliable SER system capable of emotion recognition in speech data. We address important issues such as feature extraction, model selection, data imbalance, robustness, and real-time inference using a labeled dataset of various emotional expressions in voice. To extract complicated shapes from auditory characteristics, our method combines deep learning techniques that include long-short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent units (GRU). We carefully manage the data imbalance to ensure that emotions are fairly represented in the training set, and with the implementation of our functional LSTM and GRU models in the training set, we were able to achieve the precision of 62 % and 90 %, respectively.

articleTitle: A Geometric Analysis of Shading on Agrivoltaic System: Bangladesh Perspective
abstract: In this study, a geometric shading analysis of an agrivoltaic system has been done considering land in Bangladesh. The approach has been proposed to simulate the shading length for inclined solar collectors or panels. Results show that the inclined solar panel of 100 cm height from the ground with 100 cm length and 170 cm width provides 286 cm of optimal inter-row distance between two adjacent rows. Also, considering the yearly shading pattern, it is viable to set the inter-panel distance as equal to the panel width. It is also evident that seasonal change has an impact on the shadow length. During the months of summer, the length is less, whereas it is highest in the months of winter. It is found that if the system height varies from 100 cm to 300 cm for January, it has a 208 cm length difference at solar noon time. Which is 89% higher than the length difference found in May. Therefore, 100 cm length could be an optimum value considering the height of the crops, tools, and the farmers who will work there.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of Graphene-PEN Based Flexible Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor (FPPS) for Enhanced Sensitivity
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the modelling and optimization of a graphene - polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) based flexible piezoresistive pressure sensor (FPPS). Leveraging the unique properties of graphene and PEN substrate, we achieve exceptional sensitivity in pressure detection. The analysis were done using COMSOL Multiphysics 6.0 version. The proposed sensor demonstrates significant promise for application in wearable electronics, healthcare monitoring and human machine interface.

articleTitle: Combining MTCMOS and Stack Techniques for Low-Power VLSI: A Case Study of a 4-Bit Asynchronous Up Counter
abstract: Low-power VLSI technology focuses on minimizing power consumption in integrated circuits while maintaining performance. This is crucial for extending battery life in portable devices, reducing heat generation, and improving energy efficiency. This work explores the design and implementation of a 4-bit asynchronous up counter using various low-power techniques, including CMOS, MTCMOS, Stack, and MTCMOS plus Stack. The study demonstrates that combining MTCMOS with the Stack technique provides the most advantageous results in terms of delay, power dissipation, and power-delay product (PDP). Using the 32nm Synopsys Custom Compiler technology, our experiments reveal that the MTCMOS plus Stack technique achieves a 53% reduction in power dissipation compared to the basic CMOS technique, significantly enhancing energy efficiency. Additionally, this hybrid approach reduces delay by 73.4% relative to the basic CMOS method, improving system speed and responsiveness.

articleTitle: ThreatScan-Strengthening Website Security with Predictive Analytics Using Machine Learning Model
abstract: ThreatScan is a machine learning-based approach proposed to strengthen website security by predicting potential external attacks. Motivated by the growing cyber threats and reliance on websites, ThreatScan utilizes the “ScrapingBot” at its core. This bot extracts malicious parameters from input websites, which are then fed into trained models such as decision trees, MLPs, and random forests based on their characteristics. A pipeline model is also employed, seamlessly integrating preprocessing with machine learning models like Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest for streamlined training. Then the model will predict potential threats generating lists of risks of each model as output. The Extensive evaluation demonstrates ThreatScan's effectiveness, with the decision tree model achieving 97.68% accuracy on the UNSW-NB15 dataset, the MLP model reaching 99.73% accuracy on KDD Cup 1999, the pipeline model attaining 97.55% accuracy on DDOS-Network-Logs, and the random forest model scoring 93.20% accuracy on the Malicious URL dataset. We‘ve also tested various parameters crawled by our ‘ScrapingBot’ from the nasa.gov website and have revealed significant insights. The source code and models are publicly released: ThreatScan GitHub Repository.

articleTitle: Color Image Encryption Using Many-Parameter Discrete Fractional Fourier Transforms
abstract: Color images can be divided into three channels including red, green and blue channels. Each channel is independently processed using a random phase encoding and then converted into the fractional domain through the multiple-parameter discrete fractional Fourier transform (MPDFRFT) or random discrete fractional Fourier transform (RDFRFT). Subsequently, the same procedure is repeated again. After the second random phase encoding and the second MPDFRFT (or RDFRFT), the encrypted image is obtained. All parameters, including the power parameters, random phases and the random matrices in the definition of the RDFRFT, can be used as encryption keys. Errors in decryption keys will result in errors of decrypted images. Security of the proposed encryption schemes using MPDFRFT and RDFRFT can be enhanced as compared to the existing similar encryption scheme using the discrete fractional Fourier transform (DFRFT) because there are much more parameters in both of the MPDFRFT and RDFRFT than those in the DFRFT and, from computer experimental results, sensitivity to decryption key errors for the proposed methods are both higher than the existing DFRFT method.

articleTitle: Detection of Potential Specific Learning Disabilities in Children through Handwriting Analysis Using Machine Learning
abstract: Specific learning disability refers to a variety of learning difficulties that impact an individual's capacity to acquire and apply specific academic skills, including reading, writing, mathematics, and reasoning. Learning difficulties, if not identified, can adversely affect children's overall learning experience. Early identification of learning difficulties in children is crucial for providing the necessary support and interventions to help them overcome the challenges. Conventional methods used by psychologists to diagnose learning disabilities include subjective assessments that also examine the behavioral aspects of children. However, these tests are time-consuming and im-practical for large groups of children. Therefore, an automated initial screening method can provide a cost-effective solution for identifying children at risk of learning difficulties who need further testing by specialists. In this study, we present an efficient, low-cost system for identifying children at risk by analyzing the static features of their handwritten text. We extracted six hand-writing features from data collected from typically developing children and those with clinically diagnosed learning disability. These features were used as inputs to a machine learning model to predict the risk of specific learning disability. We compared the performance of various classifiers, and the random forest classifier achieved the best results, with an accuracy of 87.3 %. These findings indicate that the model effectively detects risk in children suggesting its potential as a valuable tool for early identification of specific learning disabilities.

articleTitle: Personalized Healthcare Empowered: Federated Learning Integration with Wearable Device Data for Enhanced Patient Insights
abstract: The capacity of wearable technology to monitor health data, send alerts, improve communication, and allow easy access to information while on the road has made it popular in the healthcare industry. Sensors on wearable technology are used to assess physiological characteristics, monitoring which provides a viable way to evaluate individual healthcare. Although there are already a lot of downstream processing methods to give health interventions and detect anomalies, wearable device data contains sensitive health information so user privacy is a problem here. Federated learning addresses this by preserving user privacy while providing accurate insights by maintaining data decentral-ization, enabling model training without sharing raw data. In this paper, we present a framework based on federated learning for wearable-enabled personalized healthcare where we address its guiding principles, obstacles, and possibilities, showcasing its adaptability and potential to enhance patient insights and health care systems.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation and Analysis of Non-Linear Activation Functions for Implicit Neural Representations
abstract: Implicit Neural Representations (INR) have found applications in various sectors like health care (computed tomography) and autonomous navigation (image processing). While there are many use cases of INRs, the non-linear activation functions are a key differentiating part in such INRs. Hence, this paper provides novel FPGA based implementations of the non-linear activation functions, namely Sine, Gaussian, and Complex Gabor Wavelet and their derivatives. All three non-linear activation functions and their derivatives were designed using AMD-Xilinx Vivado HLS 2019.2 and were synthesized, run implementation, and generate bit-stream using AMD-Xilinx Vivado 2019.2. Xilinx PYNQ framework was used for validation on the target FPGA embedded platform (Avnet Ultra96 v2 - Xilinx ZU3EG Zynq Ultrascale + MPSoC). Further, a detailed comparison highlighting their importance with respect to some key parameters like silicon area, power and timing has been provided to allow design engineers and researchers working in this field to make an appropriate choice based on the application considered.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Two-Wheeler EV Batteries in Irregular Terrains
abstract: Two-wheeler Electric Vehicles are the preferred choice in many developing countries for daily commutes and cost-effective transportation purposes. The present-day EVs mainly make use of Li-ion batteries as the energy source. As the battery is the most expensive component in an EV, the optimized usage of the EV battery is crucial to prevent premature battery degradation. The battery degradation phenomenon not only depends on the battery chemistry but also on the user behaviour and driving patterns. This paper analyses the battery performance parameters in irregular terrains by using a battery model for a light electric vehicle (LEV). The reference drive cycle patterns corresponding to the irregular terrains and two standard drive cycles are used to evaluate the battery performance. A simscape model of the LEV battery is developed and its degradation behaviour is analysed in irregular terrains. Further, a quantitative comparison of SOC degradation and thermal behaviour has been conducted using the developed models and irregular drive cycle patterns.

articleTitle: Design & Analysis of Adaptive Noise Equalizer for EV Charging Infrastructure Integrated PV Systems
abstract: This article introduces a novel control algorithm for grid-connected solar photovoltaic (PV) powering EV batteries. The technology utilizes an adaptive noise equalizer (ANE) to charge electric vehicle (EV) batteries during daylight hours while improving power quality. The Electric Vehicle (EV) and Battery Energy Storage (BES) are linked together using a bidirectional buck-boost converter at the direct current (dc) link. The electric vehicle (EV) draws power from the solar array during daylight hours. When there is no sunlight or the level of irradiance is below a certain level, the EV supplies power to the grid. The control algorithm compensates for harmonic current while charging and discharging the EV battery. Additionally, it ensures that the overall harmonics distortion of the grid currents is limited to less than 5%, as recommended by the IEEE-519 standard. The VSC serves the multifunctional purpose of reactive power compensation and maintaining unity power factor operation in different G2V and V2G modes. The adaptive noise equalizer is implemented to reduce the harmonics injected into the source current by nonlinear load and maintain the sinusoidal currents. The results verify the performance of EV charging infrastructure integrated PV systems under different steady state and dynamic conditions under G2V and V2G modes.

articleTitle: Automated Wheat Rust Disease Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks With Transfer Learning
abstract: Wheat, a cornerstone crop nourishing billions globally, faces a substantial threat from various diseases. Among these, wheat rust, caused by parasitic fungi, stands out as a major cause of yield loss. Early and accurate detection of this disease plays a crucial role in minimizing crop devastation and ensuring global food security. This work explores the automatic classification of wheat diseases using transfer learning. We examine the performance of four deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that have already been trained: VGG16, MobileNet, InceptionV3, and InceptionResNetV2. These models were trained on a curated dataset encompassing three distinct classes: healthy wheat leaves, brown (leaf) rust, and yellow (strip) rust. Our investigation revealed that the proposed approach, utilizing the VGG16 model, achieved a remarkable accuracy of 97.95%. Furthermore, the model exhibited exceptional recall performance, demonstrating its ability to effectively identify diseased wheat instances. Notably, the VGG16 model achieved a perfect recall of 100% for brown rust detection and a very high recall of 96% for yellow rust. This exceptional performance underlines the effectiveness of VGG16 in accurately classifying diseased wheat plants. These findings pave the way for the utilization of transfer learning with VGG16 in real-world applications aimed at early detection of wheat rust. By enabling rapid and precise identification of diseased crops, this approach has the potential to significantly contribute to improved crop management practices, reduced losses, and ultimately, enhanced global food security.

articleTitle: A User-Friendly Reconfigurable Power Electronics Testbed System for Educational and Research Purposes
abstract: The present paper relates to a user-friendly reconfigurable testbed system that can be used in power engineering research and education to test and validate the power electronic circuits and converter systems. Input and output voltmeters and ammeters are present in the testbed to display the measured input and output voltage and current of the realized circuit. The availability of the IGBT switch modules, along with the passive circuit elements like inductors and capacitors, provides the user flexibility to realize various power electronics circuits. Any topologies requiring a maximum of twelve power electronics switches and a minimum of one switch, fixed inductors, variable inductors, and the capacitors in the given voltage and current range can be realizable by making an external electrical connection. Also, there are bulb loads and power supplies available in the testbed. The users can implement various circuits by adding their controller externally to the testbed or by using the inhouse controller of the testbed. Six voltage and current sensors are available in the testbed to sense the voltage and current of the circuit. There are voltage and current displays connected with the sensors to show the sensor voltages and currents. The reconfigurable power electronics testbed system also has features like inbuilt hardware protection from faults.

articleTitle: A Finite Element Study of SMR-Based MEMS Magnetoelectric Micro Antenna for On-Chip RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: Magnetoelectric (ME) antennas exhibit significant potential for ambient RF energy harvesting. COMSOL Multi-physics software was used to develop a 2D finite element model for an aluminum nitride (AlN)/Terefnol-D heterostructure-based solidly mounted resonator (SMR) ME antenna based on MEMS technology. The proposed SMR ME antenna with three pairs of SiO2/Mo Bragg reflector layers has a dominant resonance frequency of 1850 MHz with a bandwidth of 36 MHz and a spurious mode at 960 MHz. At 960 MHz, with an in-plane RF magnetic field perturbation of 0.9 mT, the maximum induced ME voltage was 19 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{V}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Design of a Configurable 8-Channel Analog Front-End and Single-Ended 12-Bit SAR ADC for Biomedical Signal Acquisition on 180nm CMOS Process
abstract: In this work, a 8-channel Analog Front-End (AFE) circuit has been proposed for biomedical signal recording and converting. The AFE had a broad bandwidth, low noise, adjustable gain, high input impedance, could handle a variety of sensor inputs, and convert them to digital signal for biomedical recording systems. This design was developed based on the following blocks. The Buffer or Burrent-to-Voltage converter block (BCV), which could be set to operate as a buffer or a current-to-voltage converter circuit, achieved high input impedance and work with sensor signal types. A chopper capacitively-coupled instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) was as the main amplifier stage of the AFE to reduce input-referred noise and balance the impedance of the overall AFE system. A programmable gain amplifier (PGA) allowed the overall gain of the AFE to be adjusted. A Successive Approximation Register Analog-to-Digital Converter (SAR ADC) with Single-Ended algorithm structure permited the conversion of biomedical signals after preprocessing into a high-resolution digital sequence. The suggested AFE operated in a wide frequency range of 0.5 Hz to 2 kHz with a high input impedance bigger than 2TΩ. With the lowest 100-dB CMRR and low input-referred noise of 1.8 µVrms, the AFE can achieve low noise efficiency. Moreover, the SAR ADC had an rail-to-rail input range and an output resolution of 12-bit with a maximum sampling rate of 2.5-MS/s. The ADC achieved SNDR of 57.32dB, SFDR of 62.05dB, helping to ensure that the biomedical signal after converting to digital signal with high quality. The design incorporated new features such as the BCV, the IRN, the CMRR and the ADC to achieve the diverse functions of converting in comparison to prior research.

articleTitle: Multiple Port EV Battery Charging Using Reconfigurable Input from Solar PV and Grid
abstract: In response to the growing need for sustainable energy solutions for EV battery charging, this paper integrates the solar-grid system, for multiple-port on-board charging of lithium-ion batteries. The system employs both solar photovoltaic (PV) and grid sources to charge the lithium-ion EV batteries and storage lead-acid battery bank to balance out the intermittency of the solar PV. The dual source charging optimizes energy utilization, enabling users to utilize solar energy efficiently during peak sunlight hours and seamlessly switch to grid power during periods of low solar generation. The system maximizes solar PV performance through perturb and observe methods, ensuring optimal power extraction, and implements power factor correction when utilizing grid power. The lithium-ion battery is charged using the constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV) approach using phase-shift full-bridge (PSFB) converter and high frequency transformer. The charging of EV battery utilizes multiple sources, i.e., solar, grid, and lead-acid battery. This combination maximizes utilization of solar PV power. The MATLAB simulation is employed to verify the performance of the proposed system under various availability combination of input source.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Different Feature Extractors for Parkinson's Disease Detection
abstract: For many decades, Parkinson's Disease (PD) has been a topic of discussion and research in the field of neurological disorders. It's one of the most common diseases associated with brain, but with no known cause and cure. There is no cure for the disease but with treatment of the symptoms during onset, progress of the disease can be controlled. But, an early-stage diagnosis of the disease is a must for proceeding with treatments to control the symptoms, making it a challenging task for the healthcare providers. There are many brain imaging tests like F-18 DOPA which can be helpful in diagnosing the disease, but early-stage detection can be more efficiently done using computer aided solutions. Most of these prominent solutions make use of AI based approaches which are trained over different kind of data. However, considering the image datasets there is an issue which is not yet addressed for the disease. There is a lack of comparative study on feature extraction techniques capable of handling scale and rotation invariance, the most important part for models running on image data. This work has addressed this issue by comparing performance of six different feature extractors: SIFT, ORB, KAZE, AKAZE, BRISK and FAST on a hand drawing dataset related to Parkinson's Disease.

articleTitle: Classification of EEG Signals for Telugu Vowels
abstract: This paper explores the potential of a Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) system for recognizing Telugu vocal and sub-vocal vowels, intending to improve communication for Telugu-speaking patients with neurodegenerative disorders. We propose classifying Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals gener-ated when Telugu vowels are spoken in a vocal or subvocal manner. EEG signals collected from an 8-channel EEG device underwent preprocessing, including Butterworth bandpass filtering, to enhance quality and extract relevant features. Frequency- domain features were extracted using Power Spectral Density (PSD) analysis. For classification tasks, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machine algorithms were chosen due to their robustness and high accuracy in handling complex datasets. The evaluation of our classifier included performance metrics such as average testing accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. In three-class classification, Random Forest achieved an accuracy of 73<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for vocal data and 80% for subvocal data. Gradient Boosting showed similar performance across both datasets. For four-class classification, Random Forest attained accuracy values of 81 % for vocal data and 71 % for subvocal data, while Gradient Boosting achieved 78% and 71 %, respectively. These results underscore the potential of machine learning in improving communication interfaces for Telugu-speaking individuals with neurodegenerative disorders.

articleTitle: Levy Flight Based Fire Hawk Optimizer
abstract: This paper introduces the Levy Flight based Fire Hawk Optimizer (LFHO), an enhanced variant of the Fire Hawk Optimizer (FHO). The idea for LFHO emerged from observing the limitations in the original FHO, notably its re-stricted exploration capability and its tendency to get trapped in local optima, leading to sub-optimal solutions. Our motivation was to overcome these limitations and enhance the algorithm's performance in multifaceted problems. LFHO incorporates a random walk mechanism to inject stochasticity into the search process, thus broadening the exploration scope and mitigating premature convergence issues. Additionally, the introduction of dual global best solutions facilitates a more comprehensive exploration of the solution space, while a dynamic re-initialization mechanism for global best solutions ensures adaptability to evolving search landscapes. Furthermore, a refined nearest function enhances navigation towards promising solutions with greater accuracy and efficiency. The LFHO algorithm's performance is evaluated on CEC(Congress on Evolutionary Computation) 2014 benchmark functions, demonstrating significant improvements over the original FHO in addressing complex optimization tasks.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Forward Compensation for Enhanced PLL Based Position Estimation of Syn-RL Motor Drive
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) drive systems that don't rely on speed sensors are more dependable, affordable, and stable. However, achieving precise control without sensors throughout whole speed spectrum is quite challenging. This paper presents an improved position and speed estimation using speed adaptive forward compensation based enhanced quadrature phase locked loop (AFCE-QPLL) technique. Syn-RL motor's active flux (AF) notion is used in proposed method to eradicate variations in estimated flux from cross-coupling. High-frequency noise and DC bias insensitivity of explained system improve its robustness. The presented method has less speed and position inaccuracy than traditional and methods. The presented system is integrated with solar PV array for augmenting battery performance. The battery performance and driving range of EV are enhanced by utilizing a roof-mounted solar panel while vehicle is in motion or stationery. The system is examined and verified using MATLAB for a 22-kW electric vehicle propulsion system based on a Syn-RL motor. It provides a thorough portrayal of EV dynamics, as well as motor battery's improved performance.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Finite Impulse Response Filter Architecture Design with Distributed Arithmetic Logic to Reduce Power and Area
abstract: This work elucidates a DA Technique-based reconfigurable FIR Filter Architecture (FA) along with parallel processing reducing the complexity of the traditional multiplier while simultaneously increasing the throughput of the filter. The suggested FIR filter design utilizes block-processing which allows memory reuse in a systolic architecture. The LUT stores the filter coefficients and the required Partial Products (PP) are created using OBC-DA. The proposed OBC-based DA approach then performs multiplication in the main function block of the systolic architecture of the filter. Verilog HDL is used for coding, simulation, and synthesis using the Xilinx Vivado tool. The suggested filter architecture performance metrics are better in comparison with those of conventional filter architectures.

articleTitle: Passive Islanding Detection Approach for Grid Integrated SPV System
abstract: This study presents a passive islanding detection technique (IDT) which is based on voltage ripple content at the point of common coupling (PCC) for grid integrated solar photovoltaic (SPV) system. While conventional passive detection techniques are commonly employed, they are not particularly effective at identifying islanding, especially when a minimal power mismatch exists. Furthermore, they may produce false detection in certain instances that are not islands. If islanding is not detected quickly, it may result in extremely hazardous and adverse situations. Passive detection techniques rely on power system parameters and might fail to detect islanding in certain scenarios. This research presents an efficient passive islanding detection approach for grid-integrated solar PV system. This technique employs time-domain spectral analysis to monitor the ripple component of the voltage source inverter (VSI) voltage at the PCC and identify discrepancies. In the presented research work islanding is detected when the ripple content is found to be more than a predetermined threshold level for a specific period of time. The performance of the presented method has been tested under different operating conditions. Within the given delay period of 3ms, the proposed technique was able to identify all forms of islanding cases and did not exhibit any form of non-detection zone.

articleTitle: Automated Performance Evaluation of Multiple Classification Models with Feature Selection for EEG-Based Driver Fatigue Detection
abstract: This paper presents a detailed comparative analysis of 34 classification models for detecting driver fatigue based on EEG signals. The performance of the models is evaluated based on accuracy, training time, and error rate by taking all and most informative features derived from the EEG dataset. The publicly available well-known 40-channel EEG data with ground truth of 12 healthy candidates are used for experimental work. Candidate-independent classification is accomplished by utilizing 11 significant features after extracting them from EEG signals. This research also investigates the performance of three feature selection algorithms: Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (MRMR), chi-square, and ReliefF for classifying each candidate's normal and fatigue states. Results indicate that the fine Gaussian SVM classification model is superior in accuracy (87.9%), whereas Linear Discriminant analysis has the least training time (1.76 Sec) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{PSD} \beta \mathbf{1},\ \mathbf{Std} \alpha$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Std} \beta$</tex> are the most informative features.

articleTitle: Power Management and Power Quality Control in Hybrid Unified-MIMO System Based Microgrid
